question: What happens to ship mortgages recorded under earlier maritime laws?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Ship mortgages recorded under earlier maritime laws are deemed to have been recorded under the corresponding provisions of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001, as stated in section 610(d) [4]. This means existing mortgages remain valid and are treated as if they were registered under the current law, without needing re-registration.

question: پرانے سمندری قانون کے تحت جاری جہاز کا سرٹیفکیٹ کب تک مؤثر رہتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: پاکستان مرچنٹ شپنگ آرڈیننس، 2001 کے تحت جہاز کے سرٹیفکیٹ کی مدت کا انحصار سرٹیفکیٹ کی قسم پر ہوتا ہے۔ مثال کے طور پر، ایک خصوصی تجارتی مسافر جہاز خلائی سرٹیفکیٹ ایک سال ([1]) کے لیے درست رہتا ہے، جبکہ کارگو جہاز حفاظتی سامان کے سرٹیفکیٹ 24 ماہ ([3]) کے لیے درست ہوتے ہیں۔ استثنی کے سرٹیفکیٹ قواعد و ضوابط ([2]) کے ذریعے مقرر کردہ مدت کے لیے نافذ رہتے ہیں، اور لوڈ لائن سرٹیفکیٹ کو کچھ شرائط کے تحت پانچ ماہ تک بڑھایا جا سکتا ہے ([4])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: When does a legacy depending on an uncertain event become vested?
expected_section_title: Date of vesting when legacy contingent upon specified uncertain event
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A legacy depending on an uncertain event becomes vested when the specified event occurs (if the legacy is conditional on the event happening) or when the event becomes impossible (if conditional on the event not happening). This is governed by Section 120 of the Succession Act 1925 and Section 21 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882. An exception exists if a fund is bequeathed upon attaining a particular age, and the will also provides income from the fund before that age is reached, making the interest non-contingent.

query_translation.original_query: When does a legacy depending on an uncertain event become vested?

retrieved_context.section_title: Date of vesting when legacy contingent upon specified uncertain event
retrieved_context.text: 120. Date of vesting when legacy contingent upon specified uncertain event.—(1) A legacy bequeathed in case a specified uncertain event shall happen does not vest until that event happens. (2) A legacy bequeathed in case a specified uncertain event shall not happen does not vest until the happening of that event becomes impossible. (3) In either case, until the condition has been fulfilled, the interest of the legatee is called contingent. *Exception.*— Where a fund is bequeathed to any person upon his attaining a particular age, and the will also gives to him absolutely the income to arise from the fund before he reaches that age, or directs the income, or so much of it as may be necessary, to be applied for his benefit, the bequest of the fund is not contingent. *Illustrations* *(i)* A legacy is bequeathed to D in case A, B and C shall all die under the age of 18. D has a contingent interest in the legacy until A, B and C all die under 18, or one of them attains that age.

retrieved_context.text: (ix) A leaves his farm of Sultanpur Khurd to B, if B shall convey his own farm of Sultanpur Buzurg to C. B's interest in the bequest is contingent until he has conveyed the latter farm to C. (x) A fund is bequeathed to A if B shall not marry C within five years after the testator's death. A's interest in the legacy is contingent until the condition is fulfilled by the expiration of the five years without B's having married C, or by the occurrence within that period of an event which makes the fulfilment of the condition impossible. (xi) A fund is bequeathed to A if B shall not make any provision for him by will. The legacy is contingent until B's death. (xii) A bequeaths to B 500 rupees a year upon his attaining the age of 18, and directs that the interest, or a competent part thereof, shall be applied for his benefit until he reaches that age. Where a legacy is given if a specified uncertain event shall happen and no time is mentioned in the will for the occurrence of that event, the legacy cannot take effect, unless such event happens before the period when the fund bequeathed is payable or distributable. *Illustrations* *(i)* A legacy is bequeathed to A, and, in case of his death, to B. If A survives the testator, the legacy to B does not take effect. *(ii)* A legacy is bequeathed to A, and, in case of his death without children, to B. If A survives the testator or dies in his lifetime leaving a child, the legacy to B does not take effect. *(iii)* A legacy is bequeathed to A when and if he attains the age of 18, and, in case of his death, to B. A attains the age of 18. The legacy to B does not take effect.

question: Who can be a trustee?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 10 of the Trusts Act, 1882, any person capable of holding property may be a trustee. However, if the trust involves the exercise of discretion, the trustee must be competent to contract. No one is bound to accept a trust, and acceptance can be indicated by words or acts. A disclaimer of trust within a reasonable period prevents the trust-property from vesting in the intended trustee.

retrieved_context.text: 10. Who may be trustee. Every person capable of holding property may be a trustee; but, where the trust involves the exercise of discretion, he cannot execute it unless he is competent to contract. No one bound to accept trust. No one is bound to accept a trust. Acceptance of trust. A trust is accepted by any words or acts of the trustee indicating with reasonable certainty such acceptance. Disclaimer of trust. Instead of accepting a trust, the intended trustee may, within a reasonable period, disclaim it, and such disclaimer shall prevent the trust-property from vesting in him. A disclaimer by one of two or more co-trustees vests the trust-property in the other or others, and makes him or them sole trustee or trustees from the date of the creation of the trust. ## *Illustrations* *(a)* A bequeaths certain property to B and C, his executors, as trustees for D, B and C prove A's will. question: What security may be given when execution is stayed during an appeal?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When execution is stayed during an appeal, the court may require a security bond (often involving property mortgages) to ensure restitution or payment of the decree’s value. The applicant must show sufficient cause, avoid unreasonable delay, and provide security for the decree’s due performance (as per [1][2][3][4]). If security is later deemed inadequate, the court may demand additional security or proceed with execution ([5]).

question: What should a decree-holder do when decree money is paid outside court?
expected_section_title: Payment out of Court to decree holder
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When decree money is paid outside court, the decree-holder must certify such payment or adjustment to the court executing the decree, as stated in section 2(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 [1]. This certification allows the court to record the payment formally. Additionally, if the payment is not made in the manner specified in rule 1 (e.g., through a bank or postal money order) or not made in writing, it will not be recognized by the court [1].

question: Who can represent a foreign ruler in court proceedings?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, the Federal Government may appoint persons to act as recognized agents for a foreign ruler in court proceedings. These appointed individuals can also authorize others to make appearances, applications, or perform acts on behalf of the foreign ruler as if they were parties to the case (Section 85 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908).

question: Is an agreement to do something impossible valid?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, an agreement to do something impossible is void under Pakistani law. Section 56 of the Contract Act, 1872, explicitly states that such agreements are invalid, as illustrated by examples like contracts to discover treasure by magic or marry someone who becomes insane before the marriage. Similarly, Section 36 voids agreements contingent on impossible events, regardless of whether the parties knew about the impossibility.

retrieved_context.text: 57. Reciprocal promise to do things legal, and also other things illegal. Where persons reciprocally promise, firstly, to do certain things which are legal, and, secondly, under specified circumstances, to do certain other things which are illegal, the first set of promises is a contract, but the second is a void agreement. *Illustration* A and B agree that A shall sell B a house for 10,000 rupees, but that, if B uses it as a gambling house, he shall pay A 50,000 rupees for it. The first set of reciprocal promises, namely, to sell the house and to pay 10,000 rupees for it, is a contract. The second set is for an unlawful object, namely, that B may use the house as a gambling house, and is a void agreement.

sources_shown_to_user.source_reference: Section 56 — Agreement to do impossible act
sources_shown_to_user.full_source_text: 56. Agreement to do impossible act. An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful. A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Compensation for loss through non-performance of act known to be impossible or unlawful. Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains through the non-performance of the promise. *Illustrations* *(a)* A agrees with B to discover treasure by magic. The agreement is void. *(b)* A and B contract to marry each other. Before the time fixed for the marriage, A goes mad. The contract becomes void.

question: When are issued coins legal tender for payment?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Issued coins are legal tender for payment if they have not been defaced and meet specific weight requirements. For coins issued under section 6 of the Pakistan Coinage Act, 1906, they must not have lost weight below the prescribed limit (e.g., 33.437 grams for a 3,000 rupee commemorative coin). Decimal coins (paisa 1, 2, 5, etc.) remain legal tender until the State Bank of Pakistan notifies their cessation, after which they no longer qualify [1][3].

question: When can a master or engineer's certificate be cancelled or suspended?
expected_section_title: Power of Federal Government to cancel, suspend, etc. Certificates of master, mate or engineer
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A master or engineer's certificate can be cancelled or suspended under the following circumstances: (1) If the Federal Government receives a report under section 471 or 481 and deems cancellation/suspension necessary [2], or if an international court/authority reports incompetence, misconduct, drunkenness, or failure to assist after a collision [2]. (2) If a Maritime Board finds the individual incompetent or guilty of misconduct, especially in collision cases where they failed to assist or provide required information [4]. question: What can a Collector require when an impounded document is not properly stamped?
expected_section_title: Collector's power to stamp instruments impounded
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 40 of the Stamp Act, 1899, if an impounded document is not properly stamped, the Collector can require the payment of the proper duty plus a penalty of five rupees. Additionally, the Collector may require an amount not exceeding ten times the proper duty if deemed fit. However, if the document was impounded solely due to contravention of sections 13 or 14, the penalty may be remitted entirely at the Collector’s discretion ([1]).

question: اگر دستاویز پر درست اسٹامپ لگا ہو تو کلکٹر کیا تصدیق کرتا ہے؟
expected_section_title: Collector's power to stamp instruments impounded
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: اگر کوئی دستاویز کلکٹر کے سامنے پیش کی جاتی ہے، تو وہ اس بات کی تصدیق کرتے ہیں کہ آیا اس پر'باضابطہ طور پر مہر لگا دی گئی ہے'یا'ڈیوٹی کے ساتھ چارج کرنے کے قابل نہیں ہے'(جیسا کہ [2] اور [3])۔ اس میں یہ جانچنا شامل ہے کہ آیا اسٹامپ مطلوبہ ڈیوٹی کی رقم پر پورا اترتا ہے اور آیا انسٹرومنٹ کسی چھوٹ کے تحت آتا ہے۔ کلکٹر کو اس کے چارج کی تصدیق کے لیے انسٹرومنٹ یا حلف نامے جیسے شواہد کی بھی ضرورت پڑ سکتی ہے (جیسا کہ [1] کے مطابق)۔ اگر درست ہے، تو وہ دستاویز پر توثیق کے ذریعے اس کی تصدیق کرتے ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can trust money be invested in a first mortgage of immovable property?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, trust money can be invested in a first mortgage of immovable property under section 20(e) of The Trusts Act, 1882, provided the property is not a leasehold for a term of years and its value exceeds the mortgage-money by one-third (or one-half if consisting of buildings).

answer: ٹرسٹ کی رقم ٹرسٹ ایکٹ 1882 کے سیکشن 20 میں درج سیکیورٹیز میں لگائی جا سکتی ہے، بشمول: (اے) وفاقی حکومت، صوبائی حکومتوں، یا برطانیہ کے وعدے کے نوٹ، ڈبینچر، یا اسٹاک (ضمانتوں کے ساتھ)، (بی) برطانیہ کی پارلیمنٹ کی طرف سے ہندوستان کے محصولات پر وصول کیے جانے والے بانڈز یا اینیوٹیز، (سی) ضمانت شدہ سود کے ساتھ ریلوے کمپنی کی سیکیورٹیز، اور (ڈی) ٹرسٹ انسٹرومنٹ یا ہائی کورٹ کے قواعد کے ذریعے مجاز دیگر سیکیورٹیز۔ 1949 کے بعد کی پابندیاں لاگو ہوتی ہیں (مثال کے طور پر، 1949 کے بعد میونسپل باڈی سیکیورٹیز میں کوئی سرمایہ کاری نہیں)۔ سیکشن 40 مختلف سرمایہ کاری کی اجازت دیتا ہے لیکن صرف سیکشن 20 میں مذکور اسی زمرے کے درمیان۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

retrieved_context.section_title: "Contract of guarantee", "surety", "principal debtor" and "creditor"
retrieved_context.text: 126. "Contract of guarantee", "surety", "principal debtor" and "creditor". A "contract of guarantee" is a contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default. The person who gives the guarantee is called the "surety": the person in respect of whose default the guarantee is given is called the "principal debtor", and the person to whom the guarantee is given is called the "creditor". A guarantee may be either oral or written.

retrieved_context.section_title: Surety's right to benefit of creditor's securities
retrieved_context.text: 141. Surety's right to benefit of creditor's securities. A surety is entitled to the benefit of every security which the creditor has against the principal debtor at the time when the contract of suretyship is entered into, whether the surety knows of the existence of such security or not; and, if the creditor loses, or, without the consent of the surety, parts with such security, the surety is discharged to the extent of the value of the security. ## *Illustrations* *(a)* C advances to B, his tenant, 2,000 rupees on the guarantee of A. C has also, a further security for the 2,000 rupees by a mortgage of B's furniture. C cancels the mortgage. B becomes insolvent, and C sues A on his guarantee. A is discharged from liability to the amount of the value of the furniture.

retrieved_context.section_title: Implied promise to indemnify surety
retrieved_context.text: 145. Implied promise to indemnify surety. retrieved_context.section_title: Agent's duty in conducting principal's business
retrieved_context.text: 211. Agent's duty in conducting principal's business. An agent is bound to conduct the business of his principal according to the directions given by the principal, or, in the absence of any such directions, according to the custom which prevails in doing business of the same kind at the place where the agent conducts such business. When the agent acts otherwise, if any loss be sustained, he must make it good to his principal, and, if any profit accrues, he must account for it. ### *Illustrations* *(a)* A, an agent engaged in carrying on for B a business, in which it is the custom to invest from time to time, at interest, the moneys which may be in hand, omits to make such investment. A must make good to B the interest usually obtained by such investments. *(b)* B, a broker, in whose business it is not the custom to sell on credit, sells goods of A on credit to C, whose credit at the time was very high. C, before payment, becomes insolvent. B must make good the loss to A.

retrieved_context.section_title: Skill and diligence required from agent
retrieved_context.text: 212. Skill and diligence required from agent. An agent is bound to conduct the business of the agency with as much skill as is generally possessed by persons engaged in similar business, unless the principal has notice of his want of skill. The agent is always bound to act with reasonable diligence, and to use such skill as he possesses; and to make compensation to his principal in respect of the direct consequences of his own neglect, want of skill or misconduct, but not in respect of loss or damage which are indirectly or remotely caused by such neglect, want of skill or misconduct. ### *Illustrations*

B names C, an auctioneer, to conduct the sale. C is not a sub-agent, but is A's agent for the conduct of the sale. *(b)* A authorises B, a merchant in ¹[Chittagong], to recover the moneys due to A from C & Co. retrieved_context.text: 217. Agent's right of retainer out of sums received on principal's account. retrieved_context.text: 215. Right of principal when agent deals, on his own account, in business of agency without principal's consent. retrieved_context.section_title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of acts done in good faith
retrieved_context.text: 223. Agent to be indemnified against consequences of acts done in good faith. Where one person employs another to do an act, and the agent does the act in good faith, the employer is liable to indemnify the agent against the consequences of that act, though it cause an injury to the rights of third persons. *Illustrations* *(a)* A, a decree-holder and entitled to execution of B's goods, requires the officer of the Court to seize certain goods, representing them to be the goods of B. The officer seizes the goods, and is sued by C, the true owner of the goods. A is liable to indemnify the officer for the sum which he is compelled to pay to C, in consequence of obeying A's directions.

retrieved_context.section_title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of lawful acts
retrieved_context.text: 222. Agent to be indemnified against consequences of lawful acts. The employer of an agent is bound to indemnify him against the consequences of all lawful acts done by such agent in exercise of the authority conferred upon him. *Illustrations* (*a*) B, at Singapur, under instructions from A of ¹[Chittagong] contracts with C to deliver certain goods to him. A does not send the goods to B, and C sues B for breach of contract. B informs A of the suit, and A authorizes him to defend the suit. B defends the suit, and is compelled to pay damages and costs, and incurs expenses. A is liable to B for such damages, costs and expenses.

retrieved_context.section_title: Liability of pretended agent
retrieved_context.text: 235. Liability of pretended agent. A person untruly representing himself to be the authorized agent of another, and thereby inducing a third person to deal with him as such agent, is liable, if his alleged employer does not ratify his acts, to make compensation to the other in respect of any loss or damage which he has incurred by so dealing.

retrieved_context.text: *(b)* B, a broker at ¹[Chittagong], by the orders of A, a merchant there contracts with C for the purchase of 10 casks of oil for A. Afterwards A refuses to receive the oil, and C sues B. B informs A, who repudiates the contract altogether. B defends, but unsuccessfully, and has to pay damages and costs and incurs expenses. A is liable to B for such damages, costs and expenses.

retrieved_context.section_title: Non-liability of employer of agent to do a criminal act
retrieved_context.text: 224. Non-liability of employer of agent to do a criminal act. Where one person employs another to do an act which is criminal, the employer is not liable to the agent, either upon an express or an implied promise, to indemnify him against the consequences of that Act. *Illustrations* *(a)* A employs B to beat C, and agrees to indemnify him against all consequences of the act. B thereupon beats C, and has to pay damages to C for so doing. A is not liable to indemnify B for those damages. *(b)* B, the proprietor of a newspaper, publishes, at A's request, a libel upon C in the paper, and A agrees to indemnify B against the consequences of the publication, and all costs and damages of any action in respect thereof. B is sued by C and has to pay damages, and also incurs expenses. A is not liable to B upon the indemnity.

retrieved_context.section_title: Liability of principal inducing belief that agent's unauthorized acts were authorized
retrieved_context.text: 237. Liability of principal inducing belief that agent's unauthorized acts were authorized. When an agent has, without authority, done acts or incurred obligations to third persons on behalf of his principal, the principal is bound by such acts or obligations if he has by his words or conduct induced such third persons to believe that such acts and obligations were within the scope of the agent's authority. *Illustrations* *(a)* A consigns goods to B for sale, and gives him instructions not to sell under a fixed price. C, being ignorant of B's instructions, enters into a contract with B to buy the goods at a price lower than the reserved price. A is bound by the contract. *(b)* A entrusts B with negotiable instruments endorsed in blank. B sells them to C in violation of private orders from A. The sale is good.

answer: فراہم کردہ حصوں میں'پریشان سمندری'کی اصطلاح واضح طور پر بیان نہیں کی گئی ہے۔ تاہم، پاکستان مرچنٹ شپنگ آرڈیننس، 2001 کی دفعہ 186 میں کہا گیا ہے کہ وفاقی حکومت یا کسی مجاز افسر کی طرف سے سمندری جہاز کی پریشانی کی تصدیق کرنے والا سرٹیفکیٹ'پریشان سمندری جہاز'کے طور پر ان کی حیثیت کا حتمی ثبوت ہے۔ دوسرے حصے ان کی راحت، دیکھ بھال اور وطن واپسی کے طریقہ کار پر تبادلہ خیال کرتے ہیں لیکن ایک الگ تعریف فراہم نہیں کرتے ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

retrieved_context.section_title: Relief and maintenance of distressed seamen
retrieved_context.text: 181. Relief and maintenance of distressed seamen.—(1) The Pakistan consular officer at or near the place outside Pakistan where a seaman is in distress shall, on application being made to him by or on behalf of the distressed seaman, provide in accordance with rules made in this behalf for the return of the seaman to a proper return port and also for his necessary clothing and maintenance until his arrival at such port.

retrieved_context.section_title: Power to make rules with respect to distressed seamen
retrieved_context.text: 180. Power to make rules with respect to distressed seamen.—The Federal Government may make rules with respect to the relief, maintenance and return to a proper return port of a shipwrecked seamen found in distress at any place in or out of Pakistan, and with respect to the circumstances in which and the conditions subject to which, seamen may be relieved and provided with passages, and generally for carrying out the purposes of this Chapter; and a distressed seaman shall not have any right to be relieved, maintained or sent to a proper return port except in the cases and to the extent and on the conditions as may be prescribed.

retrieved_context.section_title: Receiving distressed seamen on ships
retrieved_context.text: 183. Receiving distressed seamen on ships.—(1) The master of a Pakistani ship shall receive on board his ship and afford passage and maintenance to all distressed seamen whom he is required by the Pakistan consular officer or the Shipping Master to take on board his ship, and shall during the passage provide every such distressed seaman with accommodation equal to that normally provided for the crew of the ship and subsistence proper to the rank or rating of the said distressed seaman: Provided that the master of the ship shall not be required to receive on board his ship a distressed seaman in terms of this section if the Pakistan consular officer or the Shipping Master is satisfied that accommodation is not and cannot be made available for such seaman.

question: When can a ship's load line certificate be cancelled?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A ship's load line certificate can be cancelled by the Federal Government if: (1) material alterations affect the load lines ([1][2][4]); (2) safety fittings/appliances are not maintained as when the certificate was issued ([1][2][4]); (3) deck line/load line markings are improperly maintained ([1][2][4]); or (4) for non-Pakistani ships, if they are found plying between Pakistan and foreign ports ([3]).

question: What happens if a testator receives a specifically bequeathed debt during his lifetime?
expected_section_title: Ademption of specific bequest of right to receive something from third party
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
If a testator receives a specifically bequeathed debt during his lifetime, the legacy is adeemed to the extent of the amount received. For example, if a debt of 10,000 rupees is bequeathed to a beneficiary, and the testator receives 5,000 rupees of that debt during his lifetime, the legacy is revoked for that 5,000 rupees (as illustrated in [1] and [2]).

retrieved_context.section_title: Ademption of specific bequest of right to receive something from third party
retrieved_context.text: 154. Ademption of specific bequest of right to receive something from third party. Where the thing specifically bequeathed is the right to receive something of value from a third party, and the testator himself receives it, the bequest is adeemed. *Illustrations* (i) A bequeaths to B— "the debt which C owes me": "2, 000 rupees which I have in the hands of D": "the money due to me on the bond of E": "my mortgage on the ¹[Rahimyarkhan] factory". All these debts are extinguished in A's lifetime, some with and some without his consent. All the legacies are adeemed. *(ii)* A bequeaths to B his interest in certain policies of his life assurance. A in his lifetime receives the amount of the policies. The legacy is adeemed. 155. Ademption *pro tanto* by testator's receipt of part of entire thing specifically bequeathed. The receipt by the testator of a part of an entire thing specifically bequeathed shall operate as an ademption of the legacy to the extent of the sum so received.

The meaning of any clause in a will is to be collected from the entire instrument, and all its parts are to be construed with reference to each other. ## *Illustrations* (i) The testator gives to B a specific fund or property at the death of A, and by a subsequent clause gives the whole of his property to A. The effect of the several clauses taken together is to vest the specific fund or property in A for life, and after his decease in B; it appearing from the bequest to B that the testator meant to use in a restricted sense the words in which he describes what he gives to A. (ii) Where a testator having an estate, one part of which is called Black Acre, bequeaths the whole of his estate to A, and in another part of his will bequeaths Black Acre to B, the latter bequest is to be read as an exception out of the first as if he had said "I give Black Acre to B, and all the rest of my estate to A"

sources_shown_to_user.source_reference: Section 82 — Meaning of clause to be collected from entire will
sources_shown_to_user.full_source_text: 82. Meaning of clause to be collected from entire will. The meaning of any clause in a will is to be collected from the entire instrument, and all its parts are to be construed with reference to each other. ## *Illustrations* (i) The testator gives to B a specific fund or property at the death of A, and by a subsequent clause gives the whole of his property to A. The effect of the several clauses taken together is to vest the specific fund or property in A for life, and after his decease in B; it appearing from the bequest to B that the testator meant to use in a restricted sense the words in which he describes what he gives to A. (ii) Where a testator having an estate, one part of which is called Black Acre, bequeaths the whole of his estate to A, and in another part of his will bequeaths Black Acre to B, the latter bequest is to be read as an exception out of the first as if he had said "I give Black Acre to B, and all the rest of my estate to A"

sources_shown_to_user.full_source_text: 105. In what case legacy lapses.—(1) If the legatee does not survive the testator, the legacy cannot take effect, but shall lapse and form part of the residue of the testator's property, unless it appears by the will that the testator intended that it should go to some other person. (2) In order to entitle the representatives of the legatee to receive the legacy, it must be proved that he survived the testator. *Illustrations* *(i)* The testator bequeaths to B "500 rupees which B owes me". B dies before the testator; the legacy lapses. *(ii)* A bequest is made to A and his children. A dies before the testator, or happens to be dead when the will is made. The legacy to A and his children lapses. *(iii)* A legacy is given to A, and, in case of his dying before the testator, to B. A dies before the testator. The legacy goes to B.

question: What places can a food inspector enter to inspect food or utensils?

answer:
A food inspector can enter markets, godowns, shops, stalls, hotels, restaurants, eating-houses, and premises used for preparing, manufacturing, or storing food or utensils under sections 16 and 18 of the Cantonments Pure Food Act, 1966. This includes places where food is sold, stored, or prepared for trade or sale.

question: خوراک کا نمونہ لینے کے لیے انسپکٹر کہاں داخل ہو سکتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: ایک انسپکٹر بازاروں، گوداموں، دکانوں، اسٹالوں، ہوٹلوں، ریستورانوں، کھانے کے گھروں اور احاطے میں داخل ہو سکتا ہے جہاں کھانا ذخیرہ کیا جاتا ہے یا فروخت کیا جاتا ہے (کنٹونمنٹ پیور فوڈ ایکٹ، 1966 کی دفعہ 16 اور 18 کے تحت)۔ وہ کھانا بنانے یا کھانے کی تیاری سے متعلق آلات/برتنوں کو ذخیرہ کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والے احاطے میں بھی داخل ہو سکتا ہے (دفعہ 16)۔ کیڑے مار ادویات کے لیے، انسپکٹر ایسے احاطے میں داخل ہو سکتے ہیں جہاں وہ ذخیرہ کیے گئے ہیں، بشمول ریلوے جیسے کیریئرز سے تعلق رکھنے والے (زرعی کیڑے مار آرڈیننس، 1971، دفعہ 16)۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

A creditor can ask a legatee who received a legacy to refund the debt (as per [1]), and may recover the debt from money paid to a person under certain conditions (as per [2]). question: What does a surety promise when giving security for appeal costs?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A surety giving security for appeal costs promises to pay the costs of the appeal if the appellant defaults, using mortgaged properties as collateral. If the sale of these properties is insufficient, the surety and their legal representatives become personally liable for the remaining balance. This is outlined in [1] and [3], which detail the surety’s obligations to stand security, mortgage properties, and comply with appellate court orders.

answer: ضامن مخصوص جائیدادوں یا اس کے کسی حصے کو منتقل نہ کرنے کا وعدہ کرتا ہے اور اس بات سے اتفاق کرتا ہے کہ اگر اپیل کنندہ ڈیفالٹ کرتا ہے تو جائیدادوں کو اپیل کے اخراجات کی ادائیگی کے لیے استعمال کیا جائے گا۔ اگر جائیدادوں کی فروخت ناکافی ہے تو ضامن اور ان کے قانونی نمائندے ذاتی طور پر بقیہ بقایا رقم کا احاطہ کریں گے۔---بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: When can another party get immediate possession of land in a pending suit?
expected_section_title: When party may be put in immediate possession of land the subject-matter of suit
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under [1], another party may be put in immediate possession of land in a pending suit if the current possessor neglects to pay government revenue or rent, leading to a sale order. The claiming party can obtain possession by paying the arrears (with or without security, at the court's discretion), and the court may award the amount paid against the defaulter, including interest.

question: How is an appeal decided when several judges hear it together?
expected_section_title: Decision where appeal heard by two or more Judges
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When an appeal is heard by two or more judges under Pakistani law, the appeal is decided according to the opinion of the majority of the judges (if any). If no majority exists, the original decree is confirmed. However, if judges on the initial bench disagree on a legal point, the matter may be referred to additional judges for a decision on that specific issue, following a majority opinion among all judges who hear it [1].

question: When is a cheque drawer discharged because the cheque was presented late?
expected_section_title: When cheque not duly presented and drawer damaged thereby
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A cheque drawer is discharged if the cheque is not presented within a reasonable time and the drawer suffers actual damage due to the delay, as outlined in section 84 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. This discharge applies only if the drawer had the right to have the cheque paid at the time of presentment and was harmed by the delay. For example, if the bank fails after the drawer has funds but before the cheque is presented, the drawer is discharged, but the holder can still claim from the bank.

When cheque not duly presented and drawer damaged thereby.—(1) Where a cheque is not presented for payment within a reasonable time of its issue, and the drawer or person on whose account it is drawn had the right, at the time when presentment ought to have been made, as between himself and the banker, to have the cheque paid and suffers actual damage through the delay, he is discharged to the extent of such damage, that is to say, to the extent to which such drawer or person is a creditor of the banker to a larger amount than he would have been if such cheque had been paid. (2) In determining what is a reasonable time, regard shall be had to the nature of the instrument, the usage of trade and of bankers, and the facts of the particular case. question: Who pays a company share call that was due before the testator died?
expected_section_title: Exoneration of specific legatee's stock in joint-stock company
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
If a company share call was due before the testator's death, the testator's estate must pay it. This is specified in section 170 of the Succession Act 1925, which states that such payments due at the time of death are borne by the estate, not the legatee. Illustration (i) in [1] and example (v) in [5] both confirm this rule.

retrieved_context.section_title: Exoneration of specific legatee's stock in joint-stock company
retrieved_context.text: 170. Exoneration of specific legatee's stock in joint-stock company. In the absence of any direction in the will, where there is a specific bequest of stock in a joint-stock company, if any call or other payment is due from the testator at the time of his death in respect of the stock, such call or payment shall, as between the testators estate and the legatee, be borne by the estate; but, if any call or other payment becomes due in respect of such stock after the testator's death, the same shall, as between the testator's estate and the legatee, be borne by the legatee, if he accepts the bequest. *Illustrations* *(i)* A bequeaths to B his shares in a certain railway. At A's death there was due from him the sum of 100 rupees in respect of each share, being the amount of a call which had been duly made, and the sum of five rupees in respect of each share, being the amount of interest which had accrued due in respect of the call. These payments must be borne by A's estate.

In Pakistani law, children in a will are defined as lineal descendants in the first degree (sons and daughters) [1]. Legitimacy generally matters unless the will explicitly refers to 'illegitimate children' or the testator's intent is clear despite errors in description [3]. If the will uses general terms like 'children,' legitimate children are prioritized, but if none exist, those with the reputation of being children (even illegitimate) may be included [3]. Specific naming of illegitimate children in the will also grants them a share [2].

retrieved_context.text: 187. When acceptance of benefit given by will constitutes election to take under will. Acceptance of a benefit given by a will constitutes an election by the legatee to take under the will, if he had knowledge of his right to elect and of those circumstances which would influence the judgment of a reasonable man in making an election, or if he waives inquiry into the circumstances. *Illustrations* *(i)* A is owner of an estate called Sultanpur Khurd, and has a life interest in another estate called Sultanpur Buzurg to which upon his death his son B will be absolutely entitled. B, in ignorance of his own right to the estate of Sultanpur Buzurg, allows C to take possession of it, and enters into possession of the estate of Sultanpur Khurd. B has not confirmed the bequest of Sultanpur Buzurg to C.

question: Who is considered a refugee for evacuee deposit purposes?
expected_act_name: THE TRANSFER OF EVACUEE DEPOSITS ACT, 1956
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Transfer of Evacuee Deposits Act, 1956, a 'refugee' is defined as a person who was ordinarily resident in areas comprising India or areas occupied by India and took refuge in Pakistan due to the creation of the Dominions of Pakistan and India, or because of civil disturbances or the fear of such disturbances ([1]).

question: What is the right of subrogation in a mortgage?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The right of subrogation under Pakistani law (as per [1]) allows a person who redeems property subject to a mortgage to acquire the same rights as the original mortgagee against the mortgagor or other mortgagees. This right arises only if the mortgage is fully redeemed, and if the redemption was funded by a third party, a registered agreement is required for subrogation. It does not apply unless the mortgage is completely redeemed.

question: Can a witness be sent to civil prison for not giving security to appear in court?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, under section 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, if a witness arrested under a warrant cannot give evidence due to the absence of parties and fails to provide bail or security, the court may order their detention in civil prison. This applies specifically to witnesses brought before the court in custody.

question: What is included in an environmental impact assessment?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
An environmental impact assessment under Pakistani law includes collection of data, prediction of qualitative and quantitative impacts, comparison of alternatives, evaluation of preventive, mitigatory, and compensatory measures, formulation of environmental management and training plans, monitoring arrangements, and framing of recommendations, along with other components as may be prescribed (as defined in [1]).

question: When can a ship owner ask the High Court to set up a limitation fund?
expected_section_title: Limitation of fund and consolidation of claims against owners
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A ship owner can apply to the High Court to set up a limitation fund when the aggregate of claims arising from an occurrence exceeds or is likely to exceed the owner's liability limits under sections 541 or 542 of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001 [1][3].

retrieved_context.section_title: Limitation of fund and consolidation of claims against owners
retrieved_context.text: 545. Limitation of fund and consolidation of claims against owners.—(1) where any liability is alleged to have been incurred by the owner of a vessel in respect of claims arising out of an occurrence and the aggregate of the claims exceeds or is likely to exceed the limits of liability of the owner under sections 541 or 542, then the owner may apply to the High Court for the setting up of a Limitation Fund for the total sum representing such limits of liability. (2) The High Court, to which the application is made under sub-section (1), may determine the amount of the owner's liability and require him to deposit such amount with the High Court or furnish such security in respect of the amount as in the opinion of the High Court is satisfactory and the amount so deposited or secured shall constitute a Limitation Fund, hereinafter referred to as the Fund for the purpose of the claims referred to in sub-section (1) and shall be utilised only for the payment of such claims.

retrieved_context.section_title: Limitation of fund and consolidation of claims against owners
retrieved_context.text: (5) Where the owner establishes that he has paid in whole or in part any claim in respect of which he can limit his liability under section 536, the High Court shall place him in the same position and to the same extent in relation to the Fund as the claimant whose claim he has paid. (6) Where the owner has established that he may at a later date be requiring to pay in whole or in part, any of the claims under this Part, which could be settled from the Fund, the High Court may notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this section order that a sufficient sum may be provisionally set aside for the purpose to enable the owner to enforce his claim against the Fund at a later date in accordance with the provisions of subsection (4). (7) If the owner is entitled to make a claim against a claimant arising out of the same occurrence, their respective claims shall be set off against each other and the provisions of this Chapter shall only apply to the balance, if any.

question: حد ذمہ داری فنڈ کس مقصد کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے؟
expected_section_title: Limitation of fund and consolidation of claims against owners
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: لمٹ لائیبلٹی فنڈ کا استعمال خصوصی طور پر جہاز کے مالک کے خلاف دعووں کی ادائیگی کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے، جیسا کہ پاکستان مرچنٹ شپنگ آرڈیننس، 2001 کی دفعہ 545 (2) میں بیان کیا گیا ہے۔ یہ فنڈ اس وقت قائم ہوتا ہے جب دعووں کا مجموعہ دفعہ 541 یا 542 کے تحت مالک کی ذمہ داری کی حدود سے تجاوز کر جاتا ہے، اور ہائی کورٹ کے ذریعے دعویداروں کے درمیان ایسے دعووں کو معقول حد تک طے کرنے کا انتظام کیا جاتا ہے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can a seaman lose his lien on the ship by agreement?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a seaman cannot lose his lien on the ship by agreement, as stated in section 549(1) of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001. However, this rule does not apply to stipulations made by seamen employed on salvage service (section 549(2)).

retrieved_context.section_title: Power to make rules
retrieved_context.text: 548. Power to make rules.—The Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this chapter. 549. Seamen's lien for wages, etc.—(1) A seaman shall have a lien on the ship, and shall not by any agreement forfeit his lien on the ship, or be deprived of any remedy for the recovery of his wages to which in the absence of the agreement he would be entitled, and shall not by any agreement abandon his right to wages in case of the loss of the ship or abandon any right that he may have or obtained in the nature of salvage, and every stipulation in any agreement inconsistent with any provisions of this Ordinance, shall be void. (2) Nothing in this section shall apply to a stipulation made by the seamen belonging to any ship which according to the terms of the agreement, is to be employed on salvage service with respect to the remuneration to be paid to them for such service to be rendered by that ship to any other ship.

retrieved_context.section_title: Priorities
retrieved_context.text: 551. Priorities.—The seaman's lien under section 549 shall have precedence over all other liens or charges on the ship, and the master's lien under section 550 shall have precedence likewise except over that of a seaman.

Master's lien.—(1) The master of a ship shall, so far as the case permits, have the same rights, liens and remedies for the recovery of his wages as a seaman has under this Ordinance, or by any law or custom having the force of law. (2) The master of a ship, and every person lawfully acting as master of a ship by reason of the decease or incapacity from illness of the master of the ship, shall so far as the case permits, have the rights, liens and remedies for the recovery of disbursement or liabilities properly made or incurred by him on account of the ship as the master has for the recovery of his wages.

answer: نہیں، کوئی ملاح پاکستانی مرچنٹ شپنگ قانون کے تحت جہاز کے نقصان کے لیے رضاکارانہ طور پر اپنا اجرت کا حق نہیں چھوڑ سکتا۔ پاکستان مرچنٹ شپنگ آرڈیننس، 2001 کی دفعہ 160 (1) میں واضح طور پر کہا گیا ہے کہ اجرت کا حق اس بات پر منحصر نہیں ہے کہ مال برداری کی جاتی ہے یا نہیں، اور ملاح اجرت کے حقدار ہیں یہاں تک کہ اگر جہاز تباہ ہو جائے۔ تاہم، یہ حق مشروط ہے: اگر کوئی ملاح جہاز، کارگو اور اسٹورز کو بچانے میں ناکام رہتا ہے، تو ان کا اجرت کا دعوی ممنوع ہے۔ فراہم کردہ حصوں میں کوئی شق نہیں ہے جو کسی ملاح کو رضاکارانہ طور پر اس حق کو معاف کرنے کی اجازت دیتی ہے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What is approved crypto apparatus?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Approved crypto apparatus refers to hardware, software, or both used for converting plain text into cipher text and vice versa, which has been approved by the Federal Government and granted an accreditation certificate by the Electronic Certification Accreditation Council under the Electronic Transaction Ordinance, 2002. This definition is provided in section 2 of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Act, 1996.

question: Who is treated as the author of the telecom employees' pension trust?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Federal Government and Company are treated as the author of the telecom employees' pension trust under section 52(2) of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Act, 1996.

answer: فراہم کردہ حصوں میں'ٹیلی کمیونیکیشن ایمپلائی ٹرسٹ'کا ذکر یا وضاحت نہیں کی گئی ہے یا اس طرح کے تناظر میں مستفیدین کی وضاحت نہیں کی گئی ہے۔ یہاں زیر بحث ٹرسٹ ایکٹ 1882 عام ٹرسٹ کے اصولوں کو حل کرتا ہے لیکن صنعت سے متعلق مخصوص ٹرسٹوں کا احاطہ نہیں کرتا ہے جیسے کہ ٹیلی مواصلات میں۔---بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can the Cabinet issue telecom policy directives?
expected_section_title: Powers of the Federal Government to issue policy directives
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, the Cabinet can issue telecom policy directives. Under section 8(2A) of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Act, 1996, the Cabinet or any committee authorized by it may issue policy directives on telecom matters, provided they are not inconsistent with the Act, and these directives are binding on the Authority.

question: Who can decide a patent dispute between an employer and employee?
expected_section_title: Power of Controller or Court to determine the matter in dispute between employer and employee
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, a dispute between an employer and employee regarding a patent or invention can be decided by either the Controller (under The Patents Ordinance, 2000, section 36) or the Court. The Controller may determine the matter if both parties apply, but if the issue involves legal questions requiring judicial determination, the Court may step in. The Court or Controller may also apportion benefits between the parties if both are entitled to them, as outlined in section 36(2).

question: What are future goods in a sale contract?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, 'future goods' are defined as goods to be manufactured, produced, or acquired by the seller after the contract of sale is made (section 2(6) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930). This includes goods whose acquisition depends on a contingency that may or may not occur, as noted in section 6(2) of the same Act.

question: سامان کی فروخت میں قیمت سے کیا مراد ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: سیلز آف گڈز ایکٹ، 1930 کے تحت، فروخت کے معاہدے میں'قیمت'معاہدے کے ذریعے طے کی جا سکتی ہے، جسے فریقین کے اتفاق رائے کے لیے چھوڑ دیا جاتا ہے، یا ان کے لین دین کے طریقہ کار کے ذریعے طے کی جا سکتی ہے ([1])۔ اگر قیمت کا واضح طور پر تعین نہیں کیا جاتا ہے، تو خریدار کو'معقول قیمت'ادا کرنی ہوگی، جو کیس کے مخصوص حالات پر منحصر ہے ([1])۔ مزید برآں، اگر کوئی معاہدہ یہ بتاتا ہے کہ کوئی تیسرا فریق قیمت کا تعین کرے گا اور وہ ایسا کرنے میں ناکام رہتا ہے، تو خریدار کو معقول قیمت ادا کرنی ہوگی اگر وہ پہلے ہی سامان حاصل کر چکا ہو ([3])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can a foreign trademark owner oppose an agent's registration application?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, a foreign trademark proprietor can oppose an agent's registration application under section 90(1)(a) of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001, which states that if the proprietor opposes such an application, registration shall be refused. This applies when the application is made by an agent or representative of the proprietor in a Convention country.

answer:
Yes, a trustee can apply to a principal Civil Court for advice on managing trust property. retrieved_context.text: 34. Right to apply to Court for opinion in management of trust-property. Any trustee may, without instituting a suit, apply by petition to a principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction for its opinion, advice or direction on any present questions respecting the management or administration of the trust-property other than questions of detail, difficulty or importance, not proper in the opinion of the Court for summary disposal. A copy of such petition shall be served upon, and the hearing thereof may be attended by, such of the persons interested in the application as the Court thinks fit. The trustee stating in good faith the facts in such petition and acting upon the opinion, advice or direction given by the Court shall be deemed, so far as regards his own responsibility, to have discharged his duty as such trustee in the subject matter of the application. The costs of every application under this section shall be in the discretion of the Court to which it is made.

question: Can a food inspector destroy unsafe perishable food without consent?

answer:
Yes, under section 16(6) of the Cantonments Pure Food Act, 1966, an inspector may destroy perishable food deemed unsound or unfit for consumption without the owner's consent, provided two respectable witnesses are present. This applies specifically to perishable items.

answer: ڈسٹرکٹ کوآپریٹو کونسل میں ضلع میں قوم کی تعمیر کے محکموں کے سربراہ اور ڈسٹرکٹ کوآپریٹو فیڈریشن کے دو نمائندے شامل ہوتے ہیں۔ اگر فیڈریشن کے نمائندے دستیاب نہیں ہیں تو کونسل صرف محکموں کے سربراہوں پر مشتمل ہو سکتی ہے۔ [1]---بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا کسی اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

retrieved_context.text: 141. Legatee named as executor cannot take unless he shows intention to act as executor. If a legacy is bequeathed to a person who is named an executor of the will, he shall not take the legacy, unless he proves the will or otherwise manifests an intention to act as executor. *Illustration* A legacy is given to A, who is named an executor. A orders the funeral according to the directions contained in the will, and dies a few days after the testator, without having proved the will. A has manifested an intention to act as executor.

retrieved_context.section_title: In what case legacy lapses
retrieved_context.text: 105. In what case legacy lapses.—(1) If the legatee does not survive the testator, the legacy cannot take effect, but shall lapse and form part of the residue of the testator's property, unless it appears by the will that the testator intended that it should go to some other person. (2) In order to entitle the representatives of the legatee to receive the legacy, it must be proved that he survived the testator. *Illustrations* *(i)* The testator bequeaths to B "500 rupees which B owes me". B dies before the testator; the legacy lapses. *(ii)* A bequest is made to A and his children. A dies before the testator, or happens to be dead when the will is made. The legacy to A and his children lapses. *(iii)* A legacy is given to A, and, in case of his dying before the testator, to B. A dies before the testator. The legacy goes to B.

question: How much deposit must a purchaser pay after buying immovable property at a court sale?

A purchaser of immovable property at a court sale must pay a deposit of 25% of the purchase-money immediately after being declared the purchaser ([1], [2]). Failure to pay this deposit results in the property being re-sold forthwith.

question: What does salary mean when wages are being considered for attachment?
expected_section_title: Property liable to attachment and sale in execution of decree
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, 'salary' for attachment purposes includes total monthly emoluments (such as wages) derived from employment, excluding any allowances declared exempt from attachment under clause (l) of section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 [2][4]. This definition applies whether the employee is on duty or on leave.

question: When must a ship master give a seaman a wage account?
expected_section_title: Master to deliver account of wages
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A ship master must deliver a full account of a seaman's wages at least 24 hours before the seaman's discharge or payment off, as specified in section 149 of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001. This applies whether the seaman is discharged before the Shipping Master or not.

question: When is a grain-loaded ship treated as unsafe because of improper loading?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A grain-loaded ship is treated as unsafe due to improper loading under Pakistani law if necessary precautions to prevent grain shifting are not taken during loading in Pakistan or on a Pakistani ship (section 389(1)), or if a ship loaded outside Pakistan with improper loading enters a Pakistani port (section 389(2)). Additionally, section 394(1) allows authorities to detain ships deemed unsafe due to improper loading, and section 400 extends this to non-Pakistani ships in Pakistani ports. Approved grain loading plans (section 388) can prevent this classification.

question: If only some goods are affected, does trademark revocation cover all goods?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, trademark revocation in Pakistan applies only to the specific goods or services for which grounds for revocation exist, not all goods. This is explicitly stated in section 73(5) of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001, which limits revocation to the affected goods/services, and similarly in section 80(6) regarding invalidity declarations.

question: Can a rent controller pass an order without holding an inquiry?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a rent controller cannot pass an order without holding an inquiry. According to section 27(1) of the Cantonments Rent Restriction Act, 1963 [1], no order under sections 7, 8, 13, 15, 17, or 19 of the Act can be made by the Controller except after holding an inquiry.

question: Can parties agree on one issue for the court to decide in a lawsuit?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, parties can agree on one issue for the court to decide in a lawsuit. Under section 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ([2]), if parties agree on a question of fact or law, they may state it as an issue in writing and specify the consequences of the court’s decision, such as payment of money, delivery of property, or performance of an act. Similarly, section 1 of the same code ([6]) allows parties to enter into a written agreement to state a case for the court’s opinion, with predefined outcomes based on the court’s finding.

question: Do administrative and technical staff of a mission get privileges if they are not local residents?
expected_act_name: THE DIPLOMATIC AND CONSULAR PRIVILEGES ACT, 1972
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, administrative and technical staff of a mission who are not nationals of or permanently resident in the receiving State enjoy privileges and immunities specified in Articles 29 to 35 of the Act, except that immunity from civil and administrative jurisdiction does not extend to acts performed outside their duties. They also enjoy privileges regarding articles imported at the time of first installation [1]. Additionally, they are exempt from dues and taxes on emoluments received due to their employment [2].

question: When does interest start on a promissory note if no date is fixed?
expected_section_title: Interest or return in any other form when rate specified or not specified
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 79(b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, if a promissory note is silent about interest or does not specify the rate, interest is calculated at six percent per annum from the date of the note until the amount is paid or a suit is instituted. This applies even if no specific date for interest payment is fixed in the instrument.

question: Can a seaman reserve a specific claim when signing a release?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, a seaman can reserve a specific claim when signing a release. Under section 155(6) of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001, a seaman may exclude a specified claim from the release, and the release does not discharge that claim.

question: What goods are considered dangerous for carriage by ship?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, dangerous goods for carriage by ship include items that, due to their nature, quantity, or mode of stowage, could endanger lives, health, or the ship itself. This includes substances defined as 'explosive' under the Explosives Act, 1884, and any other goods specified by the Federal Government via official notification. However, fog signals, distress equipment, and other safety stores required by the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance are explicitly excluded from this definition ([1], [3], [4]).

question: Can a port health officer medically examine seamen on a vessel?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).

Yes, a port health officer can medically examine seamen on a vessel. Under section 17(2)(b) of The Ports Act, 1908, a health-officer has the power to enter a vessel and medically examine all or any of the seamen or apprentices on board.

Yes, a trademark with no distinctive character can be refused registration under section 14(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001. However, if the mark has acquired distinctive character through use or is a well-known trademark before the application date, registration may still be allowed.

question: Can a trademark owner sue alone when an exclusive licensee also has rights?
expected_section_title: Exclusive licensee having rights and remedies of assignee
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a trademark owner cannot sue alone when an exclusive licensee also has concurrent rights. Under section 78(4) of The Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001, the proprietor or exclusive licensee must obtain leave from the High Court or an IP Tribunal to proceed unless the other party is joined as a plaintiff or added as a defendant. This applies unless interlocutory relief is sought, which may be granted without involving the other party.

retrieved_context.text: 5. Continuous and discontinuous, apparent and non-apparent, easements. —Easements are either continuous or discontinuous, apparent or non-apparent. A continuous easement is one whose enjoyment is, or may be, continual without the act of man. A discontinuous easement is one that needs the act of man for its enjoyment. An apparent easement is one the existence of which is shown by some permanent sign which, upon careful inspection by a competent person, would be visible to him. A non-apparent easement is one that has no such sign. *Illustrations* *(a)* A right annexed to B's house to receive light by the windows without obstruction by his neighbor A. This is a continuous easement. *(b)* A right of way annexed to A's house over D's land. This is a discontinuous easement.

question: ڈمپ شدہ درآمدات پر اینٹی ڈمپنگ ڈیوٹی کس صورت میں لگائی جاتی ہے؟

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: درج ذیل معاملات میں اینٹی ڈمپنگ ڈیوٹی عائد کی جاتی ہے: (1) جب کمیشن یہ طے کرتا ہے کہ کوئی پروڈکٹ ڈمپ کیا گیا ہے اور گھریلو صنعت کو نقصان پہنچاتا ہے (سیکشن 3 [4])۔ (2) جب کمیشن کو چوٹ لگنے یا چوٹ کا خطرہ نظر آتا ہے، یا اگر عارضی اقدامات پہلے سے موجود ہیں (سیکشن 55 [1])۔ (3) عارضی اقدامات کے 90 دن کے اندر درآمدات کے لیے، اگر نقصان دہ ڈمپنگ یا بڑے پیمانے پر قلیل مدتی درآمدات سے چوٹ لگنے کی تاریخ ہے (سیکشن 54 [3] [5])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).

question: What does a food inspector do after taking a food sample for analysis?

After taking a food sample for analysis, the inspector divides the sample into three parts, seals them, and gives one part to the person from whom the sample was taken, keeps one part for future comparison, and sends the third part to the Public Analyst for examination [1]. If the sample is from imported or transit food, the part delivered to the person may be retained unless the consignor’s details are present, in which case it is sent to the consignor [1].

question: What should someone submit when asking to keep information confidential?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When requesting confidentiality, a party must submit the information along with a request for confidentiality at the time of submission, including the reasons warranting confidentiality [1][2][5][6]. They must also provide a non-confidential summary of the information, which may include ranges, indexation, or marked deletions (limited to buyer/supplier names unless otherwise allowed by the Commission) [1][2][4]. In exceptional cases, a party may state that summarization is not possible, but must explain why [3][4].

question: What certificate must a foreign passenger ship show before port clearance?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A foreign passenger ship must produce valid safety convention certificates to the officer of Customs before port clearance is granted, as required under section 355 of the Pakistan Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001. question: What incidents must be recorded in a ship official log-book?
expected_section_title: Entries required to be made in official log-book
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, a ship's official log-book must record: (1) collisions (section 416), (2) distress signals received and occasions when the master could not assist vessels/aircraft in distress (section 406 and 425), (3) crew-related matters like convictions, offences, punishments, and conduct reports (section 425), (4) medical events (illness, injury, death) and births/marriages on board (section 425), (5) crew changes, wages, and property matters (section 425), and (6) load line details, deck cargo tonnage, and Maritime Board orders (section 425). Entries must be signed by the master and crew as required (section 424).

question: Can the government authorize call interception for national security?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, under section 54(1) of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Act, 1996, the Federal Government may authorize call interception in the interest of national security or to prevent an offence, regardless of other laws. This power is explicit and does not require additional justification beyond national security concerns or the apprehension of offences.

question: What matters can Pakistan regulate in a designated continental shelf area?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).

Pakistan can regulate the exploration, development, and protection of resources in a designated continental shelf area ([1]), safety of artificial structures ([1]), marine environmental protection ([1]), customs and fiscal matters ([1]), navigation regulations ([1]), and scientific research authorization ([2]). question: When can a trademark be registered after an application is accepted?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A trademark can be registered after an application is accepted if (a) no opposition is filed within the period specified in section 28(2) or (b) all oppositions are withdrawn or decided in favor of the applicant, and the prescribed registration fee is paid. The registration takes effect from the application’s filing date, not the acceptance date [1].

Under section 45 of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001, a word can become the only practicable name of a product after a patent ends if: (1) the article/substance was manufactured under a patent that is no longer in force, (2) at least two years have passed since the patent's expiration, and (3) the word is the only practicable name for the product. This is specified in proviso (b) of section 45 [1][2].

question: Who keeps property documents when the same property is sold to different buyers?
expected_section_title: Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When the same property is sold to different buyers, the buyer of the lot of greatest value is entitled to the property documents, but they must keep the documents safe and unaltered unless prevented by fire or other inevitable accident. The seller or this buyer must also provide true copies or extracts of the documents upon request by other buyers, at the requester’s cost ([1]).

question: What payment order can be made in a foreclosure or sale decree?
expected_section_title: PRELIMINARY DECREE FOR FORECLOSURE OR SALE
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
In a foreclosure or sale decree under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the court may order that money realized from the sale be paid into court and applied in the following order: (1) to pay the plaintiff’s mortgage amount and costs of the suit, (2) to pay subsequent interest adjudged by the court, (3) to pay the defendant’s mortgage amount, and (4) any remaining balance to the defendant or other entitled persons (as detailed in sections related to preliminary and final decrees).

answer: ٹرانسفر آف پراپرٹی ایکٹ 1882 کی دفعہ 83 کے تحت، وہ رقم جو رہن دار (یا مقدمہ قائم کرنے کا حقدار کوئی شخص) عدالت میں جمع کر سکتا ہے وہ'رہن پر واجب الادا رقم'ہے۔ یہ اصل رقم واجب الادا ہونے کے بعد اور چھٹکارے کے مقدمے کی روک تھام سے پہلے لاگو ہوتا ہے۔ دفعہ 84 مزید واضح کرتی ہے کہ اصل پر سود جمع (یا ٹینڈر) کی تاریخ سے ختم ہو جاتا ہے، بشرطیکہ دفعہ 83 کی تمام شرائط پوری ہوں۔ تاہم، اگر ڈپازٹ بعد میں واپس لے لیا جاتا ہے، تو سود واپسی کی تاریخ سے دوبارہ شروع ہوتا ہے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can a fixed judgment amount be set off against a bill of exchange claim?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, a fixed judgment amount can be set off against a bill of exchange claim if both are definite pecuniary demands. For example, if A sues B on a bill of exchange for Rs.500 and B has a judgment against A for Rs.1,000, the court may allow set-off because both claims are specific monetary amounts ([1][d]). However, if the compensation claim is not ascertained (e.g., uncertain amount), set-off is not permitted ([1][c]).

question: How does the Commission check whether an indirect tax rebate gives a subsidy?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Commission checks whether an indirect tax rebate gives a subsidy by first verifying if the exporting country has a system to confirm inputs used in production (as per [1]), then examining if that system is reasonable and effective. It also assesses whether the rebate exceeds the actual indirect taxes levied on inputs consumed in the product, making normal allowance for waste ([2] and [3]). Practical tests may be conducted under section 26 if needed ([1]).

question: When is a subsidy considered specific to certain enterprises?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A subsidy is considered specific to certain enterprises if the granting authority or the legislation it operates under explicitly limits access to the subsidy to those enterprises [1]. This is outlined in section 5(2)(a) of the Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001 [2].

question: کب سبسڈی کو مخصوص اداروں تک محدود سمجھا جاتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: پاکستانی قانون کے تحت، سبسڈی کو مخصوص اداروں تک محدود سمجھا جاتا ہے اگر وہ دینے والے اتھارٹی یا قانون سازی کے ذریعہ واضح طور پر مخصوص کاروباری اداروں تک محدود ہیں، کسی نامزد جغرافیائی خطے تک محدود ہیں، یا برآمدی کارکردگی پر منحصر ہیں (چاہے وہ قانونی طور پر منسلک نہ ہوں)۔ ان شرائط کا خاکہ [1]، [2]، [3]، اور [4] میں بیان کیا گیا ہے۔---بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can a vehicle be driven on a national highway without registration?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a vehicle cannot be driven on a national highway without registration. According to section 18 of the National Highways Safety Ordinance, 2000, driving a road vehicle on a national highway is prohibited unless it is registered and displays a valid registration mark. This requirement applies unless the vehicle is exempted or being registered for the first time within the jurisdiction of a registering authority.
