indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: کیمیائی ہتھیاروں کے کنونشن کے نفاذ آرڈیننس، 2000 کے تحت، شیڈول 1 کیمیکل تیار کرنے والی چھوٹے پیمانے کی سہولت کو مخصوص تکنیکی حدود کی تعمیل کرنی ہوگی (مثال کے طور پر، رد عمل کے برتن کا سائز اور ترتیب) لیکن متن میں ایسی سہولیات کے لیے زیادہ سے زیادہ سالانہ پیداوار کی مقدار واضح طور پر نہیں بتائی گئی ہے۔ تاہم، [1] کے پیراگراف 10 اور 11 میں ذکر کیا گیا ہے کہ حفاظتی مقاصد کے لیے ہر سال 10 کلوگرام تک شیڈول 1 کیمیکل کی پیداوار کی اجازت ہے، اور تحقیق، طبی، یا دواسازی کے مقاصد کے لیے ہر سال 10 کلوگرام تک فی سہولت کی اجازت ہے، حالانکہ یہ ان سہولیات کے لیے مجموعی حدود ہیں جو [1] کے پیراگراف 8 کے تحت'واحد چھوٹے پیمانے'کے طور پر درجہ بند نہیں ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے ؛ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What privileges do chemical inspection team members receive in Pakistan?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
expected_section_title: Privileges and immunities of members of inspection team and observers
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Chemical inspection team members in Pakistan enjoy privileges and immunities similar to diplomatic agents under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961), specifically Articles 29, 30(1)-(2), 31(1)-(3), and 34, as well as paragraph 1(b) of Article 36 (except for prohibited imports/exports). Their samples and approved equipment are inviolable and exempt from customs duties ([1][2][3]). These privileges apply during inspections, transit, or when waiving immunity (if notified by the National Authority).

question: How long can someone be detained before a board must review the case?
expected_section_title: Reference to Board and its procedure
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A person can be detained for a maximum of three months before a board must review the case, as specified in sections 6A of The Security of Pakistan Act, 1952 ([1]) and section 5 of The Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977 ([2][3][4]). If detention continues beyond three months, the board must review the case again every three months.

question: When can a drug label be considered misleading or unsafe?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A drug label can be considered misleading or unsafe under the Drugs Act, 1976 if it lacks required information (like warnings or usage directions) prominently, contains false claims, or fails to mention relevant standards (e.g., pharmacopoeia). This is defined as a 'misbranded drug' in [1] and [3], and prohibited under [2].

question: Who holds an inquiry when an explosives accident causes loss of life?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When an explosives accident causes loss of life, the district Magistrate holds the inquiry under section 9 of the Explosives Act, 1884 [1]. This applies unless the accident occurs in connection with the armed forces, in which case the relevant military authority conducts the inquiry [1].

question: What can happen if a convicted person appears within sixty days after trial in absence?
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
expected_section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Court
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
If a convicted person appears within sixty days after being tried in absentia, the Special Court must set aside the conviction and proceed with the trial according to law, provided the person proves they did not abscond or conceal themselves to avoid the proceedings (as per [1] and [4]).

question: Which court tries scheduled offences committed in a zone?
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Scheduled offences committed in a zone are triable only by the Special Court exercising territorial jurisdiction in that zone, as per section 9(1) of the Act [1]. However, the Government may declare that such an offence should be tried by a Special Court established outside the zone under section 9(2) [1].

question: What activities are included in manufacturing a drug?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, manufacturing a drug includes operations such as processing, compounding, formulating, filling, packing, repacking, altering, ornamenting, finishing, and labelling, as defined in section 3(r) of the Drugs Act, 1976. However, it explicitly excludes compounding and dispensing in the ordinary course of retail business or on a prescription by a registered medical practitioner, dentist, or veterinarian.

question: What drug pricing matters can the Federal Government regulate?
expected_section_title: Power of Federal Government to make rules
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Federal Government can regulate drug pricing by prescribing measures to maintain supplies at reasonable prices, fixing prices for manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, retailers, and other dealers, and controlling bonuses given to these parties. This is outlined in section 43(v) of the Drugs Act, 1976 [1].

question: Can electric supply lines be connected with earth without permission?
expected_section_title: Prohibition of connection with earth, and power for Government to interfere in certain cases of default
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, under section 34 of the Electricity Act, 1910, no person may connect electric supply-lines to earth without permission. The Provincial Government must sanction such connections, and violations can result in orders to remedy the issue or prohibition of use until compliance. [1]

question: What safety orders can be given for vessels in port?
expected_section_title: Powers of the ¹[Chief of the Naval Staff]
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, safety orders for vessels in port can include fire safety measures, vessel operations, and port regulations. The Chief of the Naval Staff may issue orders for fire safety, vessel safety, and even scuttling or beaching vessels if necessary ([1]). The Federal Government can make orders for port safety, including dealing with explosions and fires on vessels carrying dangerous cargoes ([2]). Additionally, the Government has broad powers to make port rules regulating vessel operations, fire use, crew numbers, passage clearance, and cargo handling ([4][5][6]).

question: What is a service line in electricity supply?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A service line is an electric supply-line through which energy is, or is intended to be, supplied by a licensee to a single consumer from a distributing main or directly from the licensee's premises, or to a group of consumers on the same or adjoining premises connected to the same point on the distributing main ([1]).

question: بجلی کے حادثے کی وجہ معلوم کرنے کے لیے کون انکوائری کر سکتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: حصوں میں بجلی کے حادثات کا خاص طور پر ذکر نہیں ہے، اس لیے فراہم کردہ متن میں اس بارے میں کوئی براہ راست قانونی التزام نہیں ہے کہ اس طرح کے واقعات کی تحقیقات کون کر سکتا ہے۔ تاہم، دھماکہ خیز مواد ایکٹ کے تحت آنے والے حادثات کے لیے، وفاقی حکومت، مجسٹریٹ، یا ڈائریکٹر جنرل دھماکہ خیز مواد جیسے مقرر کردہ عہدیداروں کے ذریعے تحقیقات کی جاتی ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے ؛ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What does carriage include for transporting explosives?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Explosives Act, 1884, 'carriage' includes any carriage, wagon, cart, truck, vehicle, or other means of conveying goods or passengers by land, regardless of propulsion method [1]. This definition applies to transporting explosives by land [2].

question: When can a Special Judge issue notice about property suspected from smuggling?
expected_section_title: Notice to person holding property suspected to be acquired by smuggling
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A Special Judge can issue a notice about property suspected of being acquired by smuggling if they receive information that a person is holding such property, and after evaluating factors like the person's assets, income sources, lifestyle, and prior smuggling involvement, the judge has written reasons to believe there is sufficient ground for proceeding. The notice must specify a minimum 30-day period for the person to show cause why the property should not be forfeited to the Federal Government ([1], [2]).

question: When do inspection team members enjoy privileges and immunities in Pakistan?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
expected_section_title: Privileges and immunities of members of inspection team and observers
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Inspection team members enjoy privileges and immunities in Pakistan when they are in Pakistan (a) during routine, challenge, or assistance inspections, or (b) while in transit to or from another State Party to the Convention in connection with such inspections [1]. These privileges are specifically tied to their activities under the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Ordinance, 2000 [2].

question: Can an electricity licensee make consumer conditions without government approval?
expected_section_title: Restrictions on licensee's controlling or interfering with use of energy
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, an electricity licensee cannot make consumer conditions without government approval. Under section 21(2) of the Electricity Act, 1910 [1], any conditions imposed by a licensee must have the previous sanction of the Provincial Government (after consulting the local authority if applicable). Conditions made without such sanction are null and void [1].

A 'terrorist affected area' is an area declared as such by the Government under section 3 of the Act, based on the scale and nature of terrorist offences being committed there. This declaration is made via a notification in the official Gazette.

question: خصوصی عدالت سے کیا مراد ہے؟
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: ایک'خصوصی عدالت'سے مراد ایک ایسی عدالت ہے جو مخصوص قوانین (مثال کے طور پر دہشت گردی سے متاثرہ علاقے (خصوصی عدالتیں) ایکٹ، 1992 یا ٹریفک جرائم (خصوصی عدالتیں) آرڈیننس، 1981) کے تحت محدود دائرہ اختیار اور طریقہ کار کے قواعد کے ساتھ قائم کی گئی ہے۔ یہ ایک اہل جج (فی [1]) پر مشتمل ہے، جو نامزد زونوں میں طے شدہ جرائم ([2]) یا ٹریفک جرائم جیسے مقدمات کو خصوصی طور پر ([6]) سنبھالتا ہے، اور منفرد طریقہ کار پر عمل کرتا ہے جیسے کہ کچھ شرائط کے تحت ملزم کی موجودگی کے بغیر مقدمات کی سماعت کرنا ([4])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What offences can the Anti Narcotics Force investigate and prosecute?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Anti Narcotics Force can investigate and prosecute offences related to the preparation, production, manufacture, transportation, illicit trafficking, or smuggling of narcotics, intoxicants, and chemical precursors used in narcotics manufacturing. This includes any offence committed during these activities, attempts, conspiracies, abetment, and violations under the Control of Narcotics Substances Ordinance, 1996, or the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979 ([1]).

question: What does an emblem include for unauthorized use restrictions?
expected_act_name: THE PAKISTAN NAMES AND EMBLEMS (PREVENTION OF UNAUTHORISED USE) ACT, 1957
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, an 'emblem' includes the flag, emblem, seal, insignia, or coat-of-arms specified in the Schedule of the Pakistan Names and Emblems Act, 1957, as well as pictorial, illustrative, or colorable imitations of any such emblem (see [1]). The Schedule specifically lists items like the Pakistan flag, government seals, and emblems of international organizations (see [3]). Unauthorized use of these is prohibited (see [2] and [4]).

question: Who can revoke or change a smuggling detention order?
expected_section_title: Power to revoke or modify detention order
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 6 of The Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977, a detention order can be revoked or modified by (a) the Government that issued the order, or (b) the Federal Government if the order was made by a Provincial Government or its officer. This power is explicitly stated in [1].

Power to revoke or modify detention order.— (1) Without prejudice to the provisions of section 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 (X of 1897), a detention order may, at any time, be revoked or modified:— (a) by the Government by which such order was made; or (b) by the Federal Government if the order was made by any of its officers or by any Provincial Government or any officer of that Government. question: What is the punishment for bringing a prohibited article into prison?
expected_section_title: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited article into or from prison and communication with prisoners
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Section 42 of the Prisons Act, 1894, bringing a prohibited article into prison is punishable by imprisonment for up to six months, a fine of up to 200 rupees, or both. This applies to anyone who introduces, removes, or attempts to introduce/remove such articles, as well as prison officers who knowingly allow it.

question: What actions by a prisoner are treated as prison offences?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 45 of The Prisons Act, 1894, prison offences include: (1) wilful disobedience to prison rules, (2) assault or criminal force, (3) insulting language, (4) immoral behaviour, (5) avoiding labour, (6) refusing to work, (7) tampering with restraints, (8) idleness at work, (9) mismanaging work, (10) damaging property, (11) defacing records, (12) possessing prohibited items, (13) feigning illness, (14) false accusations, (15) failing to report emergencies, and (16) conspiring to escape. These are detailed in [1] and [2].

question: What does hirz mean in theft-related rules?
expected_act_name: THE OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY (ENFORCEMENT OF HUDOOD) ORDINANCE, 1979
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
In theft-related rules under the Offences Against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979, 'hirz' means an arrangement for the custody of property. This includes property in a house (whether the door is closed or not), in containers like an almirah or box, or in the custody of a person (paid or unpaid). If a single family lives in a house, the entire house is one 'hirz,' but if multiple families live in the same house, each family's occupied portion is a separate 'hirz' ([1]).

question: Who counts as a close relative in smuggling-related definitions?

answer:
Under the Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977, a 'relative' includes a person's spouse, brothers, sisters, siblings of the spouse, lineal ascendants or descendants (such as parents, children, grandparents), and lineal descendants of siblings. This definition is found in section 2(e) of the Act [1]. The term 'close relative' is not explicitly used, but these relationships are likely considered close for legal purposes under the statute.

answer: فراہم کردہ حصے پاکستان سے سامان کی نقل و حمل کے تناظر میں'اسمگلنگ'کی واضح طور پر وضاحت نہیں کرتے ہیں۔ وہ اسمگلنگ سے متعلق قانونی نتائج، طریقہ کار اور پابندیوں پر تبادلہ خیال کرتے ہیں (مثال کے طور پر، عادت والے مجرم، بانڈ اور عدالتی کارروائیاں) لیکن اصطلاح کے معنی کو واضح نہیں کرتے ہیں۔---بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: How much notice is needed before electrical work near a telegraph line?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Electricity Act, 1910 (section 17), a licensee must give at least 10 days' notice to the telegraph authority before laying electric supply lines within 10 yards of a telegraph line, unless it's a service line (requiring 48 hours' notice) or an emergency (requiring notice as soon as possible after the emergency arises). The Telegraph Act, 1885 (section 19A) also requires one month's notice for actions likely to damage telegraph lines, but this applies broadly to any person, not just licensees.

question: What is an extradition offence?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
An 'extradition offence' is defined in section 2(a) of the Extradition Act, 1972 as an offence whose act or omission falls within the descriptions set out in the Schedule. If the offence occurred in Pakistan, it must also constitute an offence under Pakistani law. For treaty states, it refers to offences covered by the extradition treaty, while for non-treaty states, it is specified by directions under section 4.

Treaty State.—(1) As soon as may be after the commencement of this Act, the Federal Government shall publish in the official Gazette a list of the foreign States with which an extradition treaty is in operation, specifying in respect of each such State the offences persons accused of which are, under the treaty, to be returned to or from that State. retrieved_context.text: 4. question: Which anti-terrorism cases can the Agency deal with?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) can deal with anti-terrorism cases under the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (XXVII of 1997) to the extent of cases with inter-provincial scope or entrusted by the Federal Government [1][2]. Additionally, it handles offences under the Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974 (VII of 1974) to the extent of terrorist activities [4].

question: Can a court order an offender on probation to pay compensation?
expected_section_title: Order for payment of costs and compensation
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, a court can order an offender on probation to pay compensation. Under section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960, a court making a probation order may require the offender to pay compensation or damages for loss or injury caused by the offence, provided the amount does not exceed the fine that could have been imposed for the offence.

question: What rules can be made about wireless telegraphy licences?
expected_section_title: Power of Federal Government to make rules
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 10(iii) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, the Federal Government can make rules governing the issuance, renewal, suspension, and cancellation of wireless telegraphy licenses, including their form and required payments. Section 5 further specifies that the Director-General (or authorized officers) is the authority to issue licenses, subject to conditions and payments prescribed by rules. These rules may also define the scope of 'wireless telegraphy apparatus' (section 2) and exempt certain persons or classes (section 4).

question: What purposes are allowed for chemicals under permitted purposes?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Ordinance, 2000, permitted purposes for chemicals include: (i) industrial, agricultural, research, medical, pharmaceutical, or other peaceful uses; (ii) protective purposes against toxic chemicals and chemical weapons; (iii) military uses not involving chemical weapons or their toxic properties; and (iv) law enforcement, including domestic riot control ([1]).

question: Who is considered a criminal prisoner?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A 'criminal prisoner' is defined as any prisoner duly committed to custody under the writ, warrant, or order of any Court or authority exercising criminal jurisdiction, or by order of a Court-martial, as per sections 3 of the Prisons Act, 1894 ([1] and [2]).

question: کن قیدیوں کو ایک جیل سے دوسری جیل منتقل کیا جا سکتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: جیل ایکٹ، 1894 کے تحت، قیدیوں کو جیلوں کے درمیان منتقل کیا جا سکتا ہے اگر: (1) وہ طبی لحاظ سے ہٹانے کے لیے موزوں ہیں (سیکشن 26 (2))، (2) بھیڑ بھاڑ، وبائی امراض، یا دیگر ہنگامی حالات کی وجہ سے عارضی رہائش کے لیے (سیکشن 7)، یا (3) صوبائی حکومت کی رضامندی سے اپنی سزا کے اختتام کے قریب آنے والے قیدیوں کے لیے (سیکشن 59 (22)۔ پاگل قیدیوں کو بھی واپس جیل منتقل کیا جا سکتا ہے اگر انہیں صحت مند دماغ سمجھا جائے (سیکشن 30 (2))۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا کسی اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What rules can be made about transmitting telegraph messages?
expected_section_title: Power to make rules for the conduct of telegraphs
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 7(2) of the Telegraph Act, 1885, the Federal Government may make rules governing the transmission of telegraph messages, including setting rates and conditions for transmission, precautions to prevent improper interception, preservation periods for documents, and fees for searching documents. These rules apply to telegraphs established by the Government or licensed persons.

question: Who can make rules about licences for explosives?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, the Federal Government may make rules regarding licenses for explosives in consultation with provincial governments, as specified in section 5 of the Explosives Act, 1884 ([1]). This authority allows them to regulate or prohibit the manufacture, possession, and use of explosives except under a license.

question: When can a youthful offender be sent to a reformatory school?
expected_section_title: Power of Courts to direct youthful offenders to be sent to Reformatory Schools
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A youthful offender can be sent to a Reformatory School if a court (such as the High Court, Court of Session, District Magistrate, or a specially empowered Magistrate) sentences them to imprisonment and deems them suitable for a Reformatory School [3]. Additionally, if a boy under 15 is sentenced to imprisonment, the District Magistrate may direct his transfer to a Reformatory School instead of serving the remainder of his sentence [4]. The Provincial Government determines the specific Reformatory School to which the offender is sent [2].

question: What can a Special Judge do if a forfeited bond penalty is not paid?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
If a forfeited bond penalty is not paid, the Special Judge may issue a warrant to attach and sell the person's movable or immovable property (section 25(2)). If the penalty remains unpaid after this, the judge may impose imprisonment for up to one year (section 25(4)). However, the judge may also remit part of the penalty if justified (section 25(5)).

question: What must a prison officer do when legal process is served on a prisoner?
expected_section_title: Process served to be transmitted at prisoner's request
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
When legal process is served on a prisoner, the prison officer must show and explain the process to the prisoner (as per [1] section 48(1)), endorse and sign a certificate confirming the prisoner's confinement and explanation of the process ([1] section 48(1)), and if requested by the prisoner, send a copy of the process to another person at the prisoner’s expense ([1] section 48(2)). Additionally, the officer receives the original process and a copy from the serving authority ([2] section 47).

retrieved_context.section_title: Process served to be transmitted at prisoner's request
retrieved_context.text: 48. Process served to be transmitted at prisoner's request.—(1) Every officer in charge of a prison upon whom service is made under section 47 shall, as soon as may be, cause the copy of the process deposited with him to be shown and explained to the person to whom it is directed, and shall thereupon endorse upon the process and sign a certificate to the effect that such person as aforesaid is confined in the prison under his charge and has been shown and had explained to him a copy of the process. (2) Such certificate as aforesaid shall be *prima facie* evidence of the service of the process, and, if the person to whom the process is directed requests that the copy shown and explained to him be sent to any other person and provides the cost of sending it by post, the officer in charge of the prison shall cause it to be so sent. *Miscellaneous* ¹49. question: Who has the exclusive privilege to establish and run telegraphs in Pakistan?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Federal Government of Pakistan has the exclusive privilege to establish and run telegraphs, as stated in section 4 of the Telegraph Act, 1885 [1]. This privilege includes the power to grant licenses to others under specific conditions [1].

question: What can count as improper interference with electricity supply?

answer:
Improper interference with electricity supply includes unauthorized connections or disconnections of meters, laying works without consent, using energy in ways that harm system safety/efficiency, and using energy under incorrect charging methods (as per sections 43 of the Electricity Act). These actions can result in fines up to 5 million rupees. [1][2]

question: When may an electricity licensee refuse a request for energy supply?
expected_section_title: Security for execution of works of licensee not being local authority
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
An electricity licensee may refuse a request for energy supply if they can prove to an Electric Inspector that (a) the nearest distributing main is already at full capacity, or (b) increasing the current would seriously affect other consumers' supply efficiency, for up to six months while infrastructure is amended [1]. Additionally, a licensee may refuse if a consumer outside the supply area hasn't agreed to a required minimum annual payment for separate supply [3].

question: Who must not be sold explosives?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Explosives must not be sold to anyone without a valid license granted under the rules made by the Federal Government under section 5 of the Explosives Act, 1884. The Act allows the Federal Government to regulate or prohibit the sale of explosives except under a license (see [2]).

question: What information must declarations include for Schedule 3 chemicals?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Declarations for Schedule 3 chemicals must include: (a) the chemical's name, common/trade name, structural formula, and Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) registry number; (b) approximate production amounts in specific tonnage ranges (30–200 tonnes, 200–100,000 tonnes, etc.); and (c) the purposes for which the chemical was or will be produced. This applies to both general declarations and those related to past production for chemical weapons purposes [1, 3].

question: When is hadd not enforced after a theft confession is withdrawn?
expected_act_name: THE OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY (ENFORCEMENT OF HUDOOD) ORDINANCE, 1979
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 11(a) of the Offences Against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979, *hadd* (the prescribed punishment for theft) shall not be enforced if theft is proved only by the convict's confession but the convict retracts their confession before the execution of *hadd*. In such cases, the court may order a retrial [1].

question: Can a formal warning be combined with other prison punishments?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a formal warning can only be combined with loss of privileges under the remission system and not with other punishments like penal diet, change of labour, or cellular confinement. This is explicitly stated in section 47(1) of the Prisons Act, 1894 [1], which lists exceptions to the combination of punishments.

question: What powers does a traffic Special Court have?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A traffic Special Court has the same powers as a Magistrate of the first class under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and may try traffic offences summarily (as per sections 262–265 of the Code) if it deems fit. It also has exclusive jurisdiction over traffic offences, meaning only it can try such cases (per section 4(1)).

question: How much notice is needed before electricity works along a street or railway?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Electricity Act, 1910, a licensee must give at least one month’s notice before starting works along a street or railway (unless it’s a service line or repair work). For repairs, renewals, or amendments where the character/position of existing works isn’t altered, 48 hours’ notice suffices (as per [1] and its adjacent excerpts).

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: پاکستانی قانون کے تحت، لائسنس یافتہ کو مرمت کرنے والے اتھارٹی یا ریلوے، ٹرام وے، یا دیگر متعلقہ انفراسٹرکچر کے مالک کو نیا برقی کام شروع کرنے سے کم از کم ایک ماہ قبل نوٹس دینا چاہیے جس میں سڑک یا ریلوے میں یا اس کے پار کام کرنا شامل ہے ([1])۔ تاہم، ان مرمتوں کے لیے جو موجودہ کاموں میں تبدیلی نہیں لاتے ہیں (مثال کے طور پر، تقسیم کرنے والے مین سے منسلک سروس لائنیں)، 48 گھنٹے کا نوٹس کافی ہے ([1])۔ مزید برآں، جب موجودہ بجلی کی لائنوں یا سیوروں کے قریب کام کرتے ہیں، تو لائسنس یافتہ کو مالک یا مقامی اتھارٹی کو 48 گھنٹے پہلے مطلع کرنا چاہیے ([3])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What factors can be used to charge for dishonest electricity consumption?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 26A of the Electricity Act, 1910, a licensee may charge a consumer for dishonest electricity consumption based on factors including: (a) connected load or maximum demand, (b) maximum energy consumption, (c) load factor, (d) power factor, (e) hours and time of use, and (f) the purpose of energy use. These factors are used when a meter or measuring apparatus is tampered with or unable to register energy accurately.

question: بجلی کے غلط استعمال کے حساب میں صارف کا لوڈ فیکٹر شامل ہو سکتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: جی ہاں، بجلی ایکٹ 1910 میں بیان کردہ مخصوص شرائط کے تحت صارفین کے لوڈ فیکٹر کو بجلی کے استعمال کے چارجز کے حساب میں شامل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ مثال کے طور پر، سیکشن 26 اے لائسنس یافتگان کو بے ایمانانہ طور پر تجریدی یا استعمال شدہ توانائی کے چارجز کا تعین کرتے وقت لوڈ فیکٹر پر غور کرنے کی اجازت دیتا ہے۔ اسی طرح، سیکشن 23 عام حالات میں مختلف چارجز کے لیے غور کے طور پر لوڈ فیکٹر کی اجازت دیتا ہے۔ تاہم، یہ تب ہی لاگو ہوتا ہے جب لائسنس یافتگان قانون میں بیان کردہ سیاق و سباق کی بنیاد پر اسے مناسب سمجھے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Must a bulk electricity licensee supply energy to a distributing licensee in its area?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Yes, a bulk electricity licensee must supply energy to a distributing licensee within their area of supply, even if the distributing licensee requests only a portion of the energy required for distribution, as per [1](2). However, the distributing licensee must enter into an agreement with the bulk-licensee on special terms (including a minimum annual payment) if required, and disputes over terms may be resolved by arbitration.

question: Can a film be publicly shown without certification from the Board?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a film cannot be publicly shown without certification from the Board under the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979, except for private exhibitions in residential premises that only record events in the life of the person or their family ([1]). Public exhibition of uncertified films is prohibited and punishable by law ([2]).

question: What information about wakf expenses must be provided?
expected_section_title: Obligation to furnish particulars relating to wakf
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 3 of the Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923, the mutwalli must provide an estimate of the expenses annually incurred in realizing the income of the wakf property, based on available details from the relevant period ([1][2][6]). Additionally, they must disclose the amount set apart under the wakf for specific purposes, including the mutwalli’s salary, religious activities, charity, and other uses ([1][2][6]). These requirements apply when furnishing statements to the court as mandated by the Act.

question: What can a court do if an offender breaks bond conditions?
expected_section_title: Failure to observe conditions of the bond
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
If an offender breaks bond conditions, the court may issue a warrant for their arrest or summons requiring them to appear (section 7(1)). After a hearing, if the court finds the offender in breach, it may sentence them for the original offence or impose a fine up to 1,000 rupees (section 7(3)(b)), considering compensation ordered under section 6. If the fine is unpaid, the court may proceed with sentencing (section 7(4)).

question: When can a Special Court try an offence summarily?
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
expected_section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Court
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A Special Court can try an offence summarily if the offence is a 'scheduled offence' punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years, or with fine, or both (under [1]). Additionally, under the Traffic Offences (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1981, a Special Court may try a traffic offence summarily in accordance with sections 262 to 265 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (under [3]).

question: What activities involving chemical weapons are prohibited?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
expected_section_title: Prohibition on development etc; of chemical weapon
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Ordinance, 2000, prohibited activities involving chemical weapons include: (1) developing, producing, acquiring, stockpiling, retaining, or transferring chemical weapons ([1]); (2) using chemical weapons or riot control agents as a method of warfare ([1]); (3) military preparations to use chemical weapons ([1]); (4) assisting others in prohibited activities ([1]); and (5) constructing or altering premises/equipment intended for chemical weapon production ([4]). Permitted purposes (e.g., industrial, medical, or protective uses) may exempt certain activities if they align with these categories ([2]). Violations carry up to 25 years' imprisonment ([1]).

question: When can a first-time offender be discharged after admonition?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A first-time offender may be discharged after admonition if the court determines that punishment is inexpedient and a probation order is not appropriate, considering factors like the offender's age, character, and the offence's nature ([1]). Additionally, under the Reformatory Schools Act, 1897, courts may discharge youthful offenders (including first-time offenders) after admonition if they deem it fit ([3]).

question: What kinds of rules can a reformatory school board make?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).

A reformatory school board can make rules about prohibited articles, school management, education of offenders, visits to offenders, handling prohibited items, penalties for violations, punishment of offenses, and granting employment licenses. question: What information must scheduled chemical handlers provide?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Scheduled chemical handlers in Pakistan must provide prescribed information to the National Authority at prescribed times and in prescribed forms (section 21 [1]), keep documents in Pakistan as specified, and register with the National Authority if required (section 23 [3]). Failure to comply may result in imprisonment up to two years or fines (sections 21(2) and 23(2)).

question: What counts as property acquired through smuggling?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977, 'property acquired by smuggling' is defined as property acquired (before or after the Act's commencement) by a person whose aggregate property value exceeds one lac rupees, either wholly or partly. The value is determined as the market-value at the time of acquisition, and this includes property held outside Pakistan ([1]).

question: What can a prison superintendent do for a serious prison discipline offence?
expected_section_title: Procedure on committal of heinous offence
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, if a prisoner commits a serious prison discipline offence that cannot be adequately punished by existing measures, the prison superintendent may forward the case to the District Magistrate or a first-class magistrate for inquiry and trial ([1]). The superintendent must also document the offence in the punishment book, including details like the prisoner’s name, offence, witnesses, and evidence ([3]). The magistrate may impose a sentence of up to one year in addition to existing imprisonment or apply other punishments under section 46. Importantly, no person may be punished twice for the same offence ([1]).

retrieved_context.text: 52. Procedure on committal of heinous offence. If any prisoner is guilty of any offence against prison discipline which, by reason of his having frequently committed such offences or otherwise, in the opinion of the Superintendent, is not adequately punishable by the infliction of any punishment which he has power under this Act to award, the Superintendent may forward such prisoner to the Court of the District Magistrate or of any Magistrate of the first class ¹[* * *] having jurisdiction, together with a statement of the circumstances, and such Magistrate shall thereupon inquire into and try the charge so brought against the prisoner, and, upon conviction, may sentence him to imprisonment which may extend to one year, such term to be in addition to any term for which such prisoner was undergoing imprisonment when he committed such offence, or may sentence him to any of the punishments enumerated in section 46 :

question: Can Schedule 2 chemicals be transferred to non-party states after the interim period?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, Schedule 2 chemicals cannot be transferred to non-party states after the three-year interim period. According to [1] and [2], such transfers are restricted to states parties once this period expires. During the interim, transfers to non-parties require strict end-use certificates, but after three years, this restriction becomes absolute for Schedule 2 chemicals.

question: What does selling a drug include?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Selling a drug includes selling, offering for sale, exposing for sale, having in possession for sale, and distribution, as defined in section 3 of the Drugs Act, 1976 [1][5]. This means the term 'sell' encompasses not only the act of selling but also related activities like displaying or holding a drug for sale.

answer: جعلی دوا وہ ہے جس کا لیبل یا پیکیجنگ دھوکہ دینے کے لیے کسی دوسرے مینوفیکچرر کی مصنوعات کی نقل کرتی ہے (مطابق [4])، جبکہ جعلی دوا وہ ہے جو منشیات ہونے کا جھوٹا دعوی کرتی ہے لیکن اس میں اس کا فعال جزو نہیں ہے، اصل میں حقیقی نہیں ہے، یا کسی فرضی مینوفیکچرر کا نام رکھتی ہے (مطابق [2])۔ مثال کے طور پر، جعلی دوا برانڈڈ دوا سے ملتی جلتی نظر آسکتی ہے لیکن کسی غیر مجاز مینوفیکچرر کے ذریعہ تیار کی جا سکتی ہے، اور جعلی دوا کسی حالت کا علاج کرنے کا دعوی کر سکتی ہے لیکن اس میں کوئی فعال اجزاء نہیں ہوتے ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What happens after the Registration Board registers a drug?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
After the Registration Board registers a drug, it must inform the applicant and Provincial Governments about the registration and the conditions attached to it ([1](10)). This notification is a mandatory step following successful registration.

answer: منشیات کا اندراج ایک مسئلہ ہو سکتا ہے اگر (اے) رجسٹریشن دھوکہ دہی یا غلط بیانی کے ذریعے حاصل کیا گیا تھا [1]، (بی) ایسے حالات جن کے تحت منشیات کا اندراج کیا گیا تھا اب موجود نہیں ہے [1]، (سی) رجسٹریشن کی شرائط کی خلاف ورزی ہے [1]، (ڈی) عوامی مفاد کے لیے منسوخی/معطلی کی ضرورت ہے [1]، یا (ای) منشیات رجسٹرڈ نہیں ہے یا رجسٹریشن کی شرائط کو پورا کرنے میں ناکام ہے [6]۔ رجسٹریشن بورڈ وجہ بتانے کا موقع فراہم کرنے کے بعد ان معاملات میں رجسٹریشن منسوخ/معطل کر سکتا ہے [2]۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Can a film be publicly shown in an unlicensed place?
expected_section_title: Licensing of places for exhibition of films
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, under section 8(5) of the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979, police officers may only enter and act in places that are licensed for film exhibitions. The law does not explicitly address unlicensed venues, but the focus on licensed places implies that public exhibitions must occur in licensed venues. However, certification of the film itself (section 4) is the primary legal requirement, not venue licensing. [1][2][3]

question: What details must a plant site declaration include?
expected_act_name: THE CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION IMPLEMENTATION ORDINANCE, 2000
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A plant site declaration must include: (a) the name of the plant site and its owner, (b) its precise location and address, (c) the number of plants declared, (d) for each plant, its name, owner, location within the site, main activities, whether it produces/consumes the chemical, if multi-purpose, other activities (like storage), and production capacity, and (e) details on chemicals (name, quantities, purposes, etc.) above declaration thresholds. These requirements apply to both Schedule 2 and Schedule 3 chemicals, with additional specifics for chemical weapons-related production.

question: What is included in the meaning of advertisement?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The meaning of 'advertisement' includes any notice, circular, or document displayed on a house, building, or wall, or published in newspapers/periodicals, as well as oral announcements or those using light/sound (per [1]). It also includes using a trade description in commercial documents like advertisements, invoices, or catalogues (per [5]).

question: What conditions can a local authority attach to telegraph work permission?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A local authority may attach conditions to telegraph work permission under section 12 of the Telegraph Act, 1885, including requirements for payment of expenses incurred by the authority, specifications for the time or mode of executing work, or other matters related to the work. However, they cannot impose conditions requiring the telegraph authority to pay rent or royalty for using their property (as per [1] and [2]).

question: What drug-related matters can federal rules prescribe?
expected_section_title: Power of Federal Government to make rules
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 43 of The Drugs Act, 1976, federal rules can prescribe: (1) drug specifications, testing methods, and substance limits [1]; (2) import/export licensing requirements and procedures [1]; (3) laboratory functions and sample testing protocols [1]; (4) packaging, labeling, and expiry date requirements [2]; (5) good manufacturing practices [3]; (6) sample distribution for sales promotion [3]; (7) procedures for introducing new drugs [3]; (8) registration processes and fees for drugs and licenses [3]; and (9) disposal rules for non-compliant drugs [1].

question: Is ignorance of a drug’s nature a defence in prosecution?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, ignorance of a drug’s nature is not a valid defence in prosecution under The Drugs Act, 1976, as explicitly stated in section 32(1) [1]. This provision clearly states that proving ignorance of the drug’s nature, substance, or quality does not absolve the accused from liability [1].

question: Can a consumer disconnect an electricity meter without written consent?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
No, a consumer cannot disconnect an electricity meter without written consent from the licensee. Section 26(5) of the Electricity Act, 1910 explicitly prohibits consumers from disconnecting a meter without obtaining the licensee's written consent, which must not be unreasonably withheld. Violations are also penalized under section 44(a) of the same Act, which imposes fines for such actions.

question: Which types of drugs cannot be sold or manufactured for sale?
expected_section_title: Import, manufacture and sale of drugs
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, the following types of drugs cannot be sold or manufactured for sale: (1) Spurious drugs (as defined in [5][zb], which include drugs without active ingredients or falsely labeled ones), (2) Sub-standard drugs (as defined in [5][zz], which fail to meet quality specifications), (3) Unregistered drugs after the specified date in [1][6], (4) Substances not classified as drugs but presented as such ([4][h]), and (5) Expired drugs ([3][h]). Additionally, drugs sold without proper batch numbers or warranties ([4][i] and [j]) are also prohibited.

question: کیا ایکسپائری کے بعد دوا بیچنا منع ہے؟

answer: جی ہاں، کسی دوا کو اس کی میعاد ختم ہونے کی تاریخ کے بعد فروخت کرنا ممنوع ہے۔ ڈرگس ایکٹ، 1976 کی دفعہ 43 (ایچ) کے تحت، وفاقی حکومت ان کے لیبل پر بیان کردہ میعاد ختم ہونے کی تاریخ کے بعد منشیات کی فروخت پر پابندی لگا سکتی ہے۔ مزید برآں، اسی ایکٹ کی دفعہ 23 (1) (vi) کسی بھی دوا کی میعاد ختم ہونے کی تاریخ کے بعد اس کی فروخت پر واضح طور پر پابندی عائد کرتی ہے۔'میعاد ختم ہونے کی تاریخ'کی اصطلاح سیکشن 3 (ایچ) میں اس تاریخ کے طور پر بیان کی گئی ہے جس کے بعد دوا کی فروخت جائز نہیں ہے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا کسی اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: کون سی جراثیم کش یا کیڑے مار چیزیں دوا کی تعریف میں آ سکتی ہیں؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: پاکستانی قانون کے تحت، کیڑے مار ادویات کو ڈرگ ایکٹ، 1976 کے مطابق'منشیات'کی تعریف سے واضح طور پر خارج کر دیا گیا ہے۔ خاص طور پر، زرعی کیڑے مار ادویات آرڈیننس، 1971 ([1])'کیڑے مار ادویات'کی تعریف ڈرگ ایکٹ کے تحت'منشیات'کے طور پر درجہ بند مادوں کو خارج کرنے کے طور پر کرتا ہے۔ تاہم، خود ڈرگ ایکٹ ([4] اور [6]) کیڑے مار ادویات یا کیڑے مار ادویات کی ایک مخصوص فہرست فراہم نہیں کرتا ہے جو منشیات کے طور پر اہل ہیں۔ اس طرح، ان قوانین کے تحت کسی بھی کیڑے مار دوا کو واضح طور پر منشیات کے طور پر بیان نہیں کیا گیا ہے۔ دونوں زمرے تعریف کے لحاظ سے باہمی طور پر خصوصی ہیں۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا ایک اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What powers does a Special Judge have during a smuggling inquiry?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A Special Judge has broad powers during a smuggling inquiry, including issuing summons and warrants, compelling witness attendance and document production, examining witnesses, and requiring government agencies like Customs, FIA, and Income-tax to assist (sections 14, 37, 38). They can also direct bonds to prevent smuggling (section 15) and have civil court-like powers (section 37).

question: Why can the government establish Special Courts in affected zones?
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The government can establish Special Courts in affected zones to ensure the speedy trial of scheduled offences, particularly when trials within the zone may not be fair, feasible without risking safety, or in the interest of justice. This authority is granted under section 6 of the Act, which allows the government to establish courts either within the zone or outside it, depending on the situation's exigencies [1].

question: حکومت خصوصی عدالت کس جگہ قائم کر سکتی ہے؟
expected_act_name: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1992
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: حکومت صوبے کے کسی بھی حصے میں ([1] کے تحت) یا دہشت گردی سے متاثرہ علاقوں (خصوصی عدالتیں) ایکٹ، 1992 کے تحت نامزد زونوں میں ایک خصوصی عدالت قائم کر سکتی ہے، جس میں زون سے باہر کے مقدمات کی سماعت کرنے کا اختیار ہے اگر حکومت کی طرف سے اعلان کیا جائے ([2])۔ مزید برآں، وفاقی حکومت مخصوص مقامات پر خصوصی اپیلٹ عدالتیں قائم کر سکتی ہے ([3])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: Who can apply for guardianship of a Hindu widow’s children after she remarries?
expected_section_title: Guardianship of children of deceased husband on the re-marriage of his widow
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: Under section 3 of the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act, 1856, if no guardian has been appointed by the deceased husband’s will, the father, paternal grandfather, mother of the paternal grandmother, or any male relative of the deceased husband may petition the court for guardianship of the children after the widow’s remarriage [1]. The court may then appoint a guardian to care for the children during their minority [1].

question: What punishment applies for solemnizing a minor’s marriage before fourteen days’ notice?
expected_section_title: Persons authorized to solemnize marriage(other than Clergy of Churches of Enland, Scotland or Rome);
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under the Christian Marriage Act, 1872, solemnizing a minor’s marriage within fourteen days after notice (without court authorization or sending a notice copy to the Senior Marriage Registrar) can result in imprisonment for up to five years ([2]). If the person is a Minister of Religion, the punishment is imprisonment for up to three years ([3]). The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, imposes a separate penalty of up to one month imprisonment or a fine of up to ₹1,000 for performing a child marriage, regardless of notice periods ([4]).

question: What kinds of cruelty allegations can appear in a divorce petition?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under The Divorce Act, 1869, cruelty allegations in divorce petitions can include: (1) cruelty coupled with adultery (sections 10 and 52), (2) cruelty without adultery (section 10, enabling divorce a mensa et toro), and (3) cruelty as a standalone ground for judicial separation (The Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936, section 34). These allegations must be proven through evidence, and the court may consider whether the petitioner has been guilty of cruelty toward the other party or their children.

question: Who can ask the court to regulate a guardian’s conduct?

Any person interested or the Court itself can ask the court to regulate a guardian’s conduct, as stated in section 43(1) of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 [1].

question: How can unpaid maintenance ordered for a wife be enforced?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Unpaid maintenance ordered for a wife can be enforced under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, as specified in section 40(1)(b) of the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936. Additionally, if the husband fails to comply, any person who supplies the wife with necessaries during this period may sue the husband for reimbursement of their cost. This enforcement mechanism applies specifically to orders made under this Act.

question: Where does the Marriage Registrar record notices of intended marriage?

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The Marriage Registrar records notices of intended marriage in a book called the 'Marriage Notice Book,' which is provided by the Provincial Government and kept in the Registrar's office. This is required under both the Christian Marriage Act, 1872 ([1]) and the Special Marriage Act, 1872 ([4]).

question: What is required after a Marriage Registrar issues a certificate?
expected_section_title: Solemnization of marriage after issue of certificate
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
After a Marriage Registrar issues a certificate, the person solemnizing the marriage must send the certificate to the Marriage Registrar of the district within one month of the solemnization. The Senior Marriage Registrar must then copy the certificate into a dedicated book and forward all received certificates (with required numbering and signatures) to the Registrar General of Births, Deaths and Marriages.

retrieved_context.section_title: Solemnization of marriage after issue of certificate
retrieved_context.text: 51. Solemnization of marriage after issue of certificate. After the issue of the certificate of the Marriage Registrar, or, where notice is required to be given under this Act to the Marriage Registrar for different districts, after the issue of the certificates of the Marriage Registrars for such districts, marriage may, if there be no lawful impediment to the marriage of the parties described in such certificate or certificates, be solemnized between them, according to such form and ceremony as they think fit to adopt. But every such marriage shall be solemnized in the presence of some Marriage Registrar (to whom shall be delivered such certificate or certificates as aforesaid), and of two or more credible witnesses besides the Marriage Registrar. And in some part of the ceremony each of the parties shall declare as follows, or to the like effect:− "I do solemnly declare that I know not of any lawful impediment why I, A. B., may not be joined in matrimony to C.D."

retrieved_context.section_title: Certificate and registry of marriage
retrieved_context.text: 6. Certificate and registry of marriage. Every marriage contracted under this Act shall, immediately on the solemnization thereof, be certified by the officiating priest in the form contained in Schedule II. The certificate shall be signed by the said priest, the contracting parties, or their fathers or guardians when they shall not have completed the age of twenty-one years, and two witnesses present at the marriage; and the said priest shall thereupon send such certificate together with a fee of two rupees to be paid by the husband to the Registrar of the place at which such marriage is solemnized. The Registrar on receipt of the certificate and fee shall enter the certificate in a register to be kept by him for that purpose and shall be entitled to retain the fee.

question: How can a respondent answer an adultery allegation in a divorce petition?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A respondent can answer an adultery allegation by denying the claim and praying the court to reject the petition, as shown in examples where respondents explicitly denied committing adultery with the alleged co-respondent [1]. They may also address condonation if applicable [3].

question: خاص شادی کے عمل میں نوٹس، اعتراض اور سرٹیفکیٹ سے متعلق کون سے مراحل شامل ہیں؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: عام شادی کے عمل میں شامل ہیں: (1) رجسٹرار کے پاس نوٹس داخل کرنا (اسپیشل میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 4 ؛ کرسچن میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 40)۔ (2) میرج نوٹس بک میں نوٹس کی کاپی درج کرنا (اسپیشل میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 5 ؛ کرسچن میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 40)۔ (3) اعتراضات کے لیے 14 دن کی اجازت دینا (اسپیشل میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 6)، تحریری طور پر درج کیے گئے اعتراضات کے ساتھ۔ (4) اگر کوئی اعتراض نہیں ہے تو، شادی کو انجام دینے کے لیے کارروائی کرنا۔ (5) شادی کے بعد سرٹیفکیٹ حاصل کرنا (اسپیشل میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 13)۔ اضافی قواعد میں انتظار کی مدت (کرسچن میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 40: عام معاملات کے لیے 4 دن، اگر نابالغ ملوث ہے تو 14 دن) اور نوٹس کے تقاضوں کی خلاف ورزی کرنے پر جرمانے (کرسچن میرج ایکٹ 1872، سیکشن 71)۔-- صرف اہل ذرائع حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔

question: What does desertion mean in a Parsi marriage dispute?
expected_act_name: THE PARSI MARRIAGE AND DIVORCE ACT, 1936
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
In a Parsi marriage dispute, 'desertion' means abandoning the other party to the marriage without reasonable cause and without their consent, or against their will, as defined in section 2 of the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936 [1].

A woman married under Muslim Law shall be entitled to obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage on any one or more of the following grounds, namely:— (i) that the whereabouts of the husband have not been known for a period of four years; (ii) that the husband has neglected or has failed to provide for her maintenance for a period of two years; ²[(iia) that the husband has taken an additional wife in contravention of the provisions of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961;] (iii) that the husband has been sentenced to imprisonment for a period of seven years or upwards; (iv) that the husband has failed to perform, without reasonable cause, his marital obligations for a period of three years; (v) that the husband was impotant at the time of the marriage and continues to be so; (vi) that the husband has been insane for a period of two years or is suffering from leprosy or a virulent venereal disease;

retrieved_context.text: 10. When husband may petition for dissolution. question: How can a respondent deny adultery allegations in a divorce case?

answer:
A respondent can deny adultery allegations by explicitly stating in their legal statement that they did not commit the alleged act. For example, in [1], the respondent denies committing adultery with *E.F.* and *G.H.*, and in [2], the respondent denies committing adultery with *X.Y.*. They may also argue that the petitioner condoned the alleged adultery, as seen in [1], though this is a separate defense from direct denial.

question: طلاق کی درخواست میں بدکاری کے الزام کے بارے میں کیا بیان کیا جا سکتا ہے؟
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: طلاق کی درخواست میں بدکاری کا الزام ثابت ہونے پر شادی کی تحلیل کا باعث بن سکتا ہے، لیکن عدالت درخواست گزار کے معاملے کو غیر مصدقہ، بدکاری کا ارتکاب نہ ہونے، یا درخواست گزار نے بدکاری کو معاف کر دیا یا جواب دہندگان کے ساتھ گٹھ جوڑ پایا تو درخواست کو مسترد کر سکتی ہے۔ درخواست گزار کو مبینہ بدکاری کو شریک مدعا علیہ کے طور پر نامزد کرنا چاہیے جب تک کہ مستثنیات لاگو نہ ہوں [5]، اور عدالت کو گٹھ جوڑ کی عدم موجودگی اور درخواست گزار کے بدکاری میں ملوث ہونے کی تصدیق کرنی چاہیے [12]۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ کردہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: How soon can an error in a marriage register entry be corrected?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
An error in a marriage register entry must be corrected within one month of discovering the error, as specified in section 78 of The Christian Marriage Act, 1872 [1]. This allows the registrar to make a marginal correction in the presence of the married persons or credible witnesses if they are unavailable.

retrieved_context.text: 78. Correction of errors. Every person charged with the duty of registering any marriage, who discovers any error in the form or substance of any such entry, may, within one month next after the discovery of such error, in the presence of the persons married, or, in case of their death or absence, in the presence of two other credible witnesses, correct the error, by entry in the margin, without any alteration of the original entry, and shall sign the marginal entry, and add thereto the date of such correction, and such person shall make the like marginal entry in the certificate thereof. question: What kinds of rules can be made about guardians’ accounts?
expected_section_title: Power of High Court to make rules
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 50 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the High Court may make rules regarding (e) preservation of guardians’ statements and accounts, (f) inspection of those accounts by interested persons, and (ff) audit of accounts under section 34A (including appointing auditors and setting their remuneration). These rules require approval by the provincial government and publication in the official Gazette. Additionally, section 34A allows the Court to appoint auditors and direct payment of their remuneration from the ward’s income.

expected_section_title: Power of High Court to make rules
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: گارڈینز اینڈ وارڈز ایکٹ 1890 کے تحت، ہائی کورٹ سرپرستوں کے کھاتوں کے آڈٹ کے حوالے سے قواعد بنا سکتی ہے، بشمول آڈٹ کے لیے مقرر کردہ افراد کی کلاس اور ان کے معاوضے کے پیمانے ([1])۔ مزید برآں، جب اکاؤنٹس کسی سرپرست کے ذریعے دکھائے جاتے ہیں، تو عدالت ایک آڈیٹر مقرر کر سکتی ہے اور ہدایت دے سکتی ہے کہ معاوضے کو وارڈ کی آمدنی میں سے ادا کیا جائے ([2])۔ ان قواعد کے لیے صوبائی حکومت کی منظوری اور سرکاری گزٹ میں اشاعت کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے ([1])۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: What is considered a bridal gift in marriage?
expected_act_name: THE DOWRY AND BRIDAL GIFTS (RESTRICTION) ACT, 1976
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under Pakistani law, a 'bridal gift' is defined as any property given before, at, or after the marriage by the bridegroom or his parents to the bride in connection with the marriage, but it does not include *Mehr* [1]. This means gifts from the groom’s side (not the bride’s parents) are considered bridal gifts, excluding the *Mehr* (a separate Islamic concept of dowry).

question: What bond may a court require from a guardian of property?
expected_section_title: Obligations on guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
Under section 34(a) of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, a court may require a guardian of property (other than the Collector) to give a bond to the Judge, with or without sureties as prescribed, to ensure they account for what they receive in respect of the ward’s property. This bond must be in the prescribed form.

retrieved_context.text: 26. Decree of separation obtained during absence of husband or wife may be reversed. Any husband or wife, upon the application of whose wife or husband, as the case may be, a decree of judicial separation bas been pronounced, may, at any time thereafter, present a petition to the Court by which the decree was pronounced, praying for a reversal of such decree, on the ground that it was obtained in his or her absence, and that there was reasonable excuse for the alleged desertion, where desertion was the ground of such decree. The Court may, on being satisfied of the truth of the allegations of such petition, reverse the decree accordingly ; but such reversal shall not prejudice or affect the rights or remedies which any other person would have had, in case it had not been decreed, in respect of any debts, contracts or acts of the wife incurred, entered into or done between the times of the sentence of separation and of the reversal thereof.

answer: فراہم کردہ حصوں میں پاکستانی قانون کے تحت شادی شدہ عورت کی علیحدہ جائیداد سے قرضوں یا معاہدوں کی وصولی کو واضح طور پر خطاب نہیں کیا گیا ہے۔ تاہم، جانشینی ایکٹ، 1925 (سیکشن 59) اس بات کی نشاندہی کرتا ہے کہ ایک شادی شدہ عورت اپنی زندگی کے دوران اپنی جائیداد کو وصیت کے ذریعے ٹھکانے لگا سکتی ہے، جس سے پتہ چلتا ہے کہ وہ اپنی علیحدہ جائیداد پر کنٹرول برقرار رکھتی ہے۔ منقولہ جائیداد کی مخصوص وصولی کے لیے، مخصوص ریلیف ایکٹ، 1877 (سیکشن 10) کسی شخص کو قبضہ کرنے کی اجازت دیتا ہے، حالانکہ اس میں شادی شدہ خواتین کی علیحدہ جائیداد کا واضح طور پر ذکر نہیں کیا گیا ہے۔ حتمی جواب کے لیے مزید قانونی دفعات یا سیاق و سباق کی ضرورت پڑ سکتی ہے۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
A guardian can transfer a ward’s property only with the previous permission of the Court ([1] and [2]). For testamentary guardians (appointed by will), this permission must be granted by the Court despite any restrictions in the will ([2]). For guardians appointed by the Court, the Court may also vary or extend their powers to allow such transfers if it deems it advantageous for the ward ([5]).

indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer: گارڈینز اینڈ وارڈز ایکٹ 1890 کی دفعہ 29 کے تحت، عدالت کے ذریعہ مقرر کردہ سرپرست عدالت کی پیشگی اجازت کے بغیر کسی وارڈ کی غیر منقولہ جائیداد کو فروخت کے ذریعے منتقل نہیں کر سکتا۔ اس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ عدالت کی واضح منظوری اس طرح کی فروخت کے لیے ایک ضروری شرط ہے۔ فروخت کے لیے دیگر مخصوص شرائط فراہم کردہ حصوں میں تفصیلی نہیں ہیں، لیکن عدالت اختیارات کی وضاحت یا پابندی کا اختیار برقرار رکھتی ہے (دفعہ 32) اور اکاؤنٹس یا ذمہ داریوں کی تعمیل کی ضرورت پڑ سکتی ہے (دفعہ 34)۔-- بازیافت شدہ قوانین صرف جزوی طور پر آپ کے سوال سے میل کھا سکتے ہیں۔ یہ قانونی مشورہ نہیں ہے۔ حوالہ شدہ ذرائع یا اہل وکیل کے خلاف ہر چیز کی تصدیق کریں۔

question: When do the powers of a guardian of a minor’s person end?
indexing_note: used_source_indexes are 1-based positions into retrieved_chunks, matching finalize_rag_ask (same order as chunks_to_sources / prompt [1]..[n]).
answer:
The powers of a guardian of a minor’s person end under the following circumstances: (a) by their death, removal, or discharge; (b) if the Court of Wards assumes superintendence of the ward’s person; (c) when the ward ceases to be a minor; (d) in the case of a female ward, by her marriage to a husband who is not unfit to be her guardian (or as determined by the Court if the guardian was court-appointed); or (e) if the ward’s father was unfit as guardian and subsequently becomes fit (as determined by the Court). These are outlined in [1].

Where a person other than a Collector, or than a guardian appointed by will or other instrument, has been appointed or declared by the Court to be guardian of the property of a ward, he shall not, without the previous permission of the Court,— (a) mortgage or charge, or transfer by sale, gift, exchange or otherwise, any part of the immoveable property of his ward, or (b) lease any part of that property for a term exceeding five years or for any term extending more than one year beyond the date on which the ward will cease to be a minor.

retrieved_context.section_title: Fiduciary relation of guardian to ward
retrieved_context.text: 20. Fiduciary relation of guardian to ward.—(1) A guardian stands in a fiduciary relation to his ward, and, save as provided by the will or other instrument, if any, by which he was appointed, or by this Act, he must not make any profit out of his office. (2) The fiduciary relation of a guardian to his ward extends to and affects purchases by the guardian of the property of the ward, and by the ward of the property of the guardian, immediately or soon after the ward has ceased to be a minor, and generally all transactions between them while the influence of the guardian still lasts or is recent.

retrieved_context.section_title: Title of guardian to custody of ward
retrieved_context.text: 25. Title of guardian to custody of ward.—(1) If a ward leaves or is removed from the custody of a guardian of his person, the Court, if it is of opinion that it will be for the welfare of the ward to return to the custody of his guardian, may make an order for his return, and for the purpose of enforcing the order may cause the ward to be arrested and to be delivered into the custody of the guardian. (2) For the purpose of arresting the ward, the Court may exercise the power conferred on a Magistrate of the first class by section 100 of the ³[Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898] (Act V of 1898). (3) The residence of a ward against the will of his guardian with a person who is not his guardian does not of itself terminate the guardianship.
